info.name: HYPR Passwordless APIs
info.description:
INTRODUCTION

Developers can use the HYPR Passwordless API to integrate their own applications with the HYPR platform. Standard REST server endpoints are available to perform device registrations, authenticate logins, manage users, configure RP Applications, review the audit trail, and handle administrative tasks.

Base URL

For all the HYPR Passwordless API endpoints described in this documentation, replace the base {{baseUrl}} placeholder with the URL of your HYPR Server. For example:

{{baseUrl}}/rp/api/versioned/recoverypin/retrieve

becomes

https://highlandsbank.hypr.com/rp/api/versioned/recoverypin/retrieve

Request Authorization

The HYPR Passwordless API can use Bearer or OAuth authentication, so you'll need to send a HYPR-supplied access token in the Authorization header when making requests. For example, in cURL:

--header 'Authorization: {{vault:bearer-token}}'

You can generate these access tokens in the HYPR Control Center as described here.

Note that most HYPR API requests use an access token issued for a specific RP Application. However, some API requests require an admin-level access token created under the special Control Center Admin RP Application. We recommend using Environment variables in Postman, giving them intuitive labels, and flagging them as secret before saving the Environment. For example:

  • {{token-ccadmin}} for rpAppId/appId controlCenterAdmin

  • {{token-hyprdefaultweb}} for rpAppId/appId HYPRDefaultApplication

  • {{token-hyprdefaultws}} for rpAppId/appId HYPRDefaultWorkstationApplication

Bearer access tokens generated through the Control Center have an expiration period (TTL) of 30 days. Note that the expiration date is reset to the current date+TTL each time you use the token, so if you access the API at least once a month the token won't expire. If you don't use the token for more than 30 days, it will expire and you'll need to generate a new one.

OAuth tokens generated through the Control Center have a default expiration period (TTL) of 1 hour (3599 seconds); this duration is set when the token is created.

item.name: Control Center
Proxy Server

request.description:
Retrieve the proxy settings used to route traffic through a proxy for Firebase PUSH.

This call only works using the controlCenterAdmin Bearer Token.

Added in HYPR version 3.8.0.

Status Codes

200 OK

Response Body

{
  "proxies": [
    {
      "protocol": "<string>",
      "host": "<string>",
      "port": "<string>",
      "user": "<string>",
      "pass": "<string>"
    }
  ]
}

protocol
The protocol used to communicate with the proxy.
[ http | https ]

host
The host where the proxy is running, without https://.

port
The port on which the proxy is running.

user
The username required for login on the proxy.

pass
The (redacted) password required for login on the proxy.

response.name: OK

request.description:

This call only works using the controlCenterAdmin Bearer Token.

Added in HYPR version 3.8.0.

Status Codes

200 OK

Request Body

protocol
The protocol used to communicate with the proxy.
[ http | https ]

host
The host where the proxy is running.

port
The port on which the proxy is running.

user
The username required for login on the proxy.

pass
The password required for login on the proxy

Response Body

There is no Response Body; the Status Code determines success or failure.

Test whether traffic can be routed from the HYPR Server to a test URL via the Proxy Server.

This call only works using the controlCenterAdmin Bearer Token.

Added in HYPR version 3.8.0.

Status Codes

200 OK

Request Body

protocol
The protocol used to communicate with the proxy.
[ http | https ]

host
The host where the proxy is running.

port
The port on which the proxy is running.

user
The username required for login on the proxy.

pass
The password required for login on the proxy.

Response Body

[
  {
    "testURL": "string",
    "configValid": boolean,
    "serviceResponse": "string",
    "errorMsg": "string"
  }
]

testURL
The URL to try to reach via the proxy server, hardcoded to https://google.com.

configValid
A flag which indicates success or failure in routing traffic through the proxy server.

serviceResponse
The HTML page received from testURL if traffic was successfully routed through the proxy server to testURL. If configValid is false, then serviceResponse is null.

errorMsg
The error message received if traffic could not be routed successfully through the proxy server to testURL. if configValid is true, then errorMsg is null.

response.name: OK

request.description:
List all Event handlers for the tenant.

The Bearer Token must be the controlCenterAdmin token.

Added in HYPR version 9.0.0.

Status Codes

200 OK
Indicates success.

Request Body

The Request Body is empty.

Response Body

[
    {
        "id": "<string>",
        "tenantUuid": "<string>",
        "name": "<string>",
        "description": "<string>",
        "version": <long> ,
        "weight": <integer>,
        "type": "<string>",
        "contentType": "<string>",
        "content": "<string>",
        "status": "<string>",
        "hyprManaged": <boolean>,
        "configuration": { "<string>" },
        "configurationMetadata": { "<string>"},
        "cronSchedule": "<string>",
        "createdAt": <datetime>,
        "createdBy": "<string>"
    },
    {
      ...
    }
]

id
The unique identifier for the handler.

tenantUuid
The universal unique identifier for the tenant.

name
The handler name.

description
A description for the handler.

version
A date-formatted version for the handler.

weight
The priority given to this policy; higher values mean higher priority.

type
The type of handler.
[ ACTION_EXECUTOR | DATA_COLLECTOR | EVENT_ENRICHER ]

contentType
Is the content BUILT_IN or CUSTOM?

content
The actual code for the handler.

status
Is the handler currently ACTIVE or DISABLED?

hyprManaged
Boolean value indicating whether or not the handler is managed by HYPR.
[ true | false ]

configuration
A map of key/value pairs containing runtime configuration values for the handler. These attributes can be retrieved by the handler code via the ctx.getConfig() call.

Adapt will treat a key as sensitive if the name:

  • contains ‘key’

  • contains ‘secret’

  • contains ‘token'

  • begins with ‘pass’

Secrets in configuration can be saved via the UI, but they will not be returned to the UI on the read calls. Instead, a string will be returned. Handler authors should name secret keys with one of these, to avoid leaks on the admin UI.

Actual secret values will still be available to the handler at runtime.

configurationMetadata
Additional key/value pairs affecting the configuration.

cronSchedule
Only used if type is set to DATA_COLLECTOR. If used, the handler will fire an action event at the scheduled time; the handler responds to the action event.

The action event is named based on the handler name. Pseudocode:

handlerName.upppercase().replace(" ", "-").replace("_", "-").append("_TRIGGER")

For example: the trigger event name for a handler named my handler is MY_HANDLER_TRIGGER.

createdAt
The Epoch timestamp when this handler was created.

createdBy
The HYPR username who created the handler.

response.name: 200 OK

item.name: Create a new Event Handler for the tenant.

request.description:
Create a new Event Handler for the tenant using minimal attributes. After completing this call, use the PATCH call to update the handler more thoroughly.

The Bearer Token must be the controlCenterAdmin token.

Added in HYPR version 9.0.0.

Status Codes

200 OK
Indicates Success

Request Body Parameters

name
The human-readable name for the handler.

content
Base64 JavaScript code to be run for this handler. Without the encoding the request will trip API security scanners.

description
A description of the handler.

status
Is the handler ACTIVE or DISABLED?

weight
The priority given to this policy; higher values mean higher priority.

configuration
A map of key/value pairs containing runtime configuration values for the handler. These attributes can be retrieved by the handler code via the ctx.getConfig() call.

Adapt will treat a key as sensitive if the name:

  • contains ‘key’

  • contains ‘secret’

  • contains ‘token'

  • begins with ‘pass’

Secrets in configuration can be saved via the UI, but they will not be returned to the UI on the read calls. Instead, a string will be returned. Handler authors should name secret keys with one of these, to avoid leaks on the admin UI.

    "eventHandlerId": "<string>",

    "lambdaRequestId": "<string>"
}

The unique identifier assigned to the handler.

version
A date-formatted version for the handler.

lambdaRequestId
A trace identifier used to determine the specific invocation run by this API call.

Test a Handler Event by submitting test data values.

The Bearer Token must be the controlCenterAdmin token.

item.description:
Create custom Event handlers to augment data and trigger actions.

See the article in our Product Documentation for a full description of HYPR Adapt Event Handlers.

request.description:
Send generic/custom Events to HYPR Adapt.

The Bearer Token must be the controlCenterAdmin token.

Added in HYPR version 9.5.0

Status Codes

204
Indicates success.

Path Parameters

  • source
    JSON path of an attribute in the Request Body, to be used as the originating source of this event. If the attribute does not exist, the value of the URL parameter is used as-is.

  • eventName
    JSON path of an attribute in the Request Body, to be used as the name of this event. If the attribute does not exist, the value of the URL parameter is used as-is.

  • entityIdOrName
    JSON path of an attribute in the Request Body, to be used as the entity name or Id. This the entity (browser, device, etc.) associated with the event.

Request Body Parameters

Valid JSON payload representing the event being sent.

myattribute
The entity attribute to be queried.

myuser
The target user associated with the entity.

nestedData
An array of nested entity attributes.

  • mynestedattr: User-defined entity attribute.

  • version: The version of the entity in question.

  • provider: The name of the entity's provider or vendor.

Example

The call /rp/api/signal/generic/nestedData.provider/MyAuthEvent/myuser is processed as follows:

  • source - nestedData.provider is resolved to microsoft

  • eventName - MyAuthEvent is not an attribute of the body, hence used as-is

  • entityIdOrName - myuser is resolved to Joe Citizen

The event is now tagged and saved as MyAuthEvent from microsoft, foruser Joe Citizen

Response Body

The Response Body is empty. See Status Codes for success/failure indications.

item.name: Create or update HYPR Adapt policies.

request.description:
Create and update policies in AWS for a specific tenant, specified by tenantUuid.

If the policyId does not match an existing policy, the call will create a new policy with the stated policyId.

The Bearer Token must be the controlCenterAdmin token.

Added in HYPR version 8.7.0.

Status Codes

200 OK
Indicates success.

Request Body Parameters

name
The name of the policy.

description
The description of the policy.

status
The current status of the policy.
[ ACTIVE | DISABLED ]

policyContentType
Determines if the policy is generated by CC (BUILT_IN; taken from the policyConfigurations property herein) or not (CUSTOM; uses the content attribute instead).
[ BUILT_IN | CUSTOM ]

policyType
Using a policy already associated with the rpAppId, determine to which operation this policy will be applied.
[ PRE_WEB_AUTH | PRE_FIDO_AUTH | PRE_FIDO2_AUTH | PRE_WORKSTATION_UNLOCK | POST_WEB_AUTH | POST_FIDO_AUTH | POST_WORKSTATION_UNLOCK | PRE_AUTH_INTEGRATIONS | POST_AUTH_INTEGRATIONS ]

weight
The relative priority of the policy. Higher values have higher priority.

metadata
Additional information about the policy.

createdBy
The user who created the policy.

policyConfigurations
An array containing configuration settings, mirroring basic Adapt Risk Policy settings in Control Center. All 4 configurations must be submitted if there is not a full policy engine script added manually.

  • numberOfFailures: The number of failures permitted before a used is blocked.

  • numericalTimeoutLength: The number of incrementOfTimeout before a user can attempt to login again.

  • incrementOfTimeout: A unit of measurement to qualify numericalTimeoutLength. [ seconds | minutes | hours | days ]

  • allowQRWhenUserIsBlocked: Determined whether or not blocked users are still permitted to authenticate using a QR code. [ true | false ]

Response Body

{
    "message": "<string>",
    "awsRequestId": "<string>"
}

message
A unique identifier appended with VER version timestamp and saved as a copied reference to the created policy. This policy can be found by both it's original policyId and the VER value on returned in the response.

awsRequestId: A unique identifier assigned to the Amazon Web Services (AWS) request.

Performs policy evaluation for a given user's authentication. The policyId and requested lifecycle will be used from the associated rpAppId, determined by the Bearer Token.

The Bearer Token determines the affected RP application; this may be the controlCenterAdmin token.

Added in HYPR version 9.0.0.

Status Codes

200 OK

Request Body

userName
The user name or entityId for whom we are making the policy evaluation request.

supportingEntities
Additional entityId(s) to lookup stored data on. All events for these entities will be passed to the policy.

For example, an IP address and/or deviceId may be passed in. Adapt looks up any event data it has on these and provides to the policy evaluation.

evaluationPoint
The evaluation point at which this policy will be executed by Control Center (CC). This will be one of the following values:

  • PRE_WEB_AUTH

    • Web pre-authentication

    • For OOB/QR flows, this is invoked before the push message is sent, to block push bombing

    • For FIDO2, this is invoked on assertions/options, since there is no other pre-step for FIDO2

  • POST_WEB_AUTH

    • Web post-authentication

    • On /rp/api/oob/client/authentication/requests/{requestId} and request status == COMPLETED

  • PRE_FIDO_AUTH

    • HYPR Mobile App pre-authentication

    • On fido/get/auth

  • POST_FIDO_AUTH

    • HYPR Mobile App post-authentication

    • On fido/send/auth

  • PRE_FIDO2_AUTH

    • FIDO2 Passkey pre-authentication

    • On fido2/assertion/options

  • POST_FIDO2_AUTH

    • FIDO2 Passkey post-authentication

    • On fido2/assertion/result

  • PRE_AUTH_INTEGRATIONS and POST_AUTH_INTEGRATIONS

    • Track the policy check before/after an authentication request from a HYPR integration

    • For example:

      • Keycloak calls the PRE evaluation point before it displays the authentication options; these are special in that these are not invoked by CC directly -- only when a policy evaluation is requested on these points via API

    • Note: In Keycloak, the POST evaluation point call is not implemented yet

  • PRE_WORKSTATION_UNLOCK

    • At the start of the workstation unlock request

      • On /client/authorize/unlock

  • POST_WORKSTATION_UNLOCK

    • At the start of the workstation unlock request

      • On client/authorization/complete/{sessionId}

      • On client/verification/complete/{sessionId}

policyId
If you created a custom policy not linked to an app, you can provide the policyId directly. In this case the evaluationPoint attribute is not needed.

The evaluationPoint approach is recommended. It avoids hard coding the policyId into API clients.

data
Optional, discretionary data sent along with the policy. This will be passed to the risk engine and can be used for decision making.

Response Body

CC will look up its config to see which policy is associated to the RPApp for the policyLifeCycle (PRE_FIDO_AUTH).

If no policy is found, nothing happens

If a policy is found, Adapt is invoked and the result is proxied back.

item.name: Affirm
Verification Flows

request.description:
Endpoint

POST {{baseUrl}}/cc/api/idv/verification

Creates a new identity verification flow configuration.

Authentication

Type: Bearer token

  • Required scope (one of):

    • scope: hypr:cc:applications (with principal = CC_ADMIN_RPAPP_ID)

    • scope: hypr:affirm:admin

    • scope: hypr:affirm:writeVerificationFlow

Request Headers

Header Required Value
Content-Type Yes application/json
Authorization Yes Bearer

Request Body

Content-Type: application/json

Constraints:

  • displayName: required, max 30 characters

  • description: optional, max 255 characters when provided

  • frictionLevel: must be NONE for this endpoint (use /verification/friction for other levels)

Request Body Schema

{
  "id": "string (optional, omit for new flow)",
  "displayName": "string (required, max 30)",
  "description": "string (optional, max 255)",
  "status": "ENABLED | DISABLED",
  "type": "ONBOARDING | RECOVERY | CC_ADMIN | CUSTOM",
  "frictionLevel": "NONE",
  "steps": [
    {
      "name": "VerificationStepName",
      "settings": {
        "VerificationStepSetting": "string value"
      }
    }
  ],
  "approvers": [
    {
      "email": "string",
      "phoneNumber": "string",
      "countryCode": "string (Alpha-2 or Alpha-3)",
      "approverType": "MANAGER | SOMEONE_ELSE | DYNAMIC | NONE",
      "oidcClientConfigId": "string",
      "inviteNextApproverAfterMinutes": 0
    }
  ],
  "escalationApprovers": [],
  "rpAppIdReference": "string",
  "codeCustomizations": {},
  "oidcClientConfigId": "string",
  "escalateToLiveChat": false,
  "contentCustomizationId": "string",
  "policyKitId": "string",
  "dataRetentionSettings": {
    "documentBiometricPolicy": "ONE_DAY | SEVEN_DAYS"
  },
  "blockDurationMins": 0,
  "workflowAttemptLimit": 10,
  "workflowAttemptWindowMins": 0,
  "imageWritebackRotationIntervalDays": 0,
  "imageWritebackRotationIntervalUnitUi": "days"
}

Field defaults

Field Default
status ENABLED
type CUSTOM
frictionLevel NONE
approvers / escalationApprovers []
escalateToLiveChat false
blockDurationMins 0
workflowAttemptLimit 10
workflowAttemptWindowMins 0
approverType SOMEONE_ELSE
inviteNextApproverAfterMinutes 0
policyKitId null
dataRetentionSettings.documentBiometricPolicy SEVEN_DAYS
imageWritebackRotationIntervalDays 0
imageWritebackRotationIntervalUnitUi "days"

Field descriptions

Top-level fields

Field Type Required Default Description
id string No null Verification flow ID for updates. Omit for new flows.
displayName string Yes — Display name for the verification flow (max 30 characters).
description string No null Description of the verification flow (max 255 characters).
status enum No ENABLED Status of the verification flow: ENABLED, DISABLED.
type enum No CUSTOM Workflow type: ONBOARDING, RECOVERY, CC_ADMIN, CUSTOM.
frictionLevel enum No NONE Friction level. Must be NONE for this endpoint; use /verification/friction for others. Values: NONE, HIGHEST, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW, LOWEST.
steps array Yes — List of verification steps in the workflow. Each step has name (VerificationStepName) and optional settings (map of setting name to string value).
approvers array No [] List of approvers for the workflow.
escalationApprovers array No [] List of escalation approvers.
rpAppIdReference string No null Reference to RP App ID.
codeCustomizations map No null Map of code customization types to customization IDs.
oidcClientConfigId string No null OIDC client configuration ID.
escalateToLiveChat boolean No false Enable escalation to live chat.
contentCustomizationId string No null Content customization kit ID.
policyKitId string No null Policy kit ID reference.
dataRetentionSettings object No null Data retention settings for document biometric data.
dataRetentionSettings.documentBiometricPolicy enum No SEVEN_DAYS Retention policy for document biometric data: ONE_DAY, SEVEN_DAYS.
blockDurationMins long No 0 Block duration in minutes.
workflowAttemptLimit integer No 10 Maximum workflow attempt limit.
workflowAttemptWindowMins long No 0 Workflow attempt window in minutes.
imageWritebackRotationIntervalDays integer No 0 Image writeback rotation interval in days.
imageWritebackRotationIntervalUnitUi string No "days" Unit label for the image writeback rotation interval (UI display only).

Step object (items in steps)

Field Type Required Description
name enum Yes One of the verification step names. See Verification step names below.
settings object No Map of step setting names to string values. Keys depend on step name; see Step settings by type below.

Approver fields (items in approvers and escalationApprovers)

Field Type Required Default Description
email string No null Approver email address.
phoneNumber string No null Approver phone number.
countryCode string No null Approver country code in Alpha-2 or Alpha-3 format (e.g. "US", "GBR").
approverType enum No SOMEONE_ELSE Approver type: MANAGER, SOMEONE_ELSE, DYNAMIC, NONE.
oidcClientConfigId string No null OIDC client configuration ID for approver authentication.
inviteNextApproverAfterMinutes integer No 0 Minutes to wait before inviting the next approver.

Verification step names

Value Description
LOGIN_ID Login identifier step
CUSTOM Custom step
PHONE_OR_EMAIL Phone or email verification step
LOCATION Location verification step
DOCUMENT_BIOMETRIC Document and biometric step
DOCUMENT_LIVENESS Document liveness check step
VERIFIED_CREDENTIAL Verified credential step
CHAT Chat escalation step
ATTESTATION Approver attestation step
OUTCOME Success outcome step
FAILURE_OUTCOME Failure outcome step

Deprecated: IDV — use DOCUMENT_BIOMETRIC.

Step settings format

Format Rule / example
Booleans Send as strings "true" or "false".
Numbers Send as strings, e.g. "1", "10".
IP lists JSON string, e.g. "[{\"rule\":\"192.168.1.0/24\",\"description\":\"Corporate Network\"}]".

request.description:
Endpoint

POST {{baseUrl}}/cc/api/idv/verification/friction

Creates a new identity verification flow with a predefined friction level (HIGHEST, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW, or LOWEST). The server generates workflow steps and approvers from the friction level and workflow type. You do not send steps, approvers, or escalationApprovers in the request. For flows with no friction, use POST {{baseUrl}}/cc/api/idv/verification instead.

Authentication

Type: Bearer token

  • Required scope (one of):

    • scope: hypr:cc:applications (with principal = CC_ADMIN_RPAPP_ID)

    • scope: hypr:affirm:admin

    • scope: hypr:affirm:writeVerificationFlow

Request Headers

Header Required Value
Content-Type Yes application/json
Authorization Yes Bearer

Request Body

Content-Type: application/json

Constraints:

  • displayName: required, max 30 characters

  • description: optional, max 255 characters when provided

  • frictionLevel: must not be NONE. Allowed: HIGHEST, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW, LOWEST.

Request Body Schema

{
  "displayName": "string (required, max 30)",
  "description": "string (optional, max 255)",
  "status": "ENABLED | DISABLED",
  "type": "ONBOARDING | RECOVERY | CC_ADMIN | CUSTOM",
  "frictionLevel": "HIGHEST | HIGH | MEDIUM | LOW | LOWEST",
  "rpAppIdReference": "string (optional)"
}

Field defaults

Field Default
status DISABLED
type CUSTOM
rpAppIdReference null

Field descriptions

Field Type Required Default Description
displayName string Yes — Display name for the verification flow (max 30 characters).
description string No null Description of the verification flow (max 255 characters).
status enum No DISABLED Status of the flow: ENABLED, DISABLED.
type enum No CUSTOM Workflow type; influences which steps and approvers the server generates: ONBOARDING, RECOVERY, CC_ADMIN, CUSTOM.
frictionLevel enum Yes — Friction level. Must be HIGHEST, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW, or LOWEST. NONE is not allowed for this endpoint.
rpAppIdReference string No null Reference to RP App ID.

Response

The response body is the created verification flow object. It includes an id assigned by the server and the full workflow: steps, approvers, and escalationApprovers generated from the requested frictionLevel and type.

Content-Type: application/json

Response body schema

{
  "id": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "displayName": "string",
  "description": "string",
  "status": "ENABLED | DISABLED",
  "type": "ONBOARDING | RECOVERY | CC_ADMIN | CUSTOM",
  "frictionLevel": "HIGHEST | HIGH | MEDIUM | LOW | LOWEST",

    {
      "name": "VerificationStepName",
      "settings": { "VerificationStepSetting": "string value" }
    }
  ],
  "approvers": [
    {
      "email": "string",
      "phoneNumber": "string",
      "countryCode": "string",
      "approverType": "MANAGER | SOMEONE_ELSE | DYNAMIC | NONE",
      "oidcClientConfigId": "string",
      "inviteNextApproverAfterMinutes": 0
    }
  ],
  "escalationApprovers": [],
  "rpAppIdReference": "string",
  "codeCustomizations": {},
  "oidcClientConfigId": "string",
  "escalateToLiveChat": false,
  "contentCustomizationId": "string",
  "policyKitId": "string",
  "dataRetentionSettings": {
    "documentBiometricPolicy": "ONE_DAY | SEVEN_DAYS"
  },
  "blockDurationMins": 0,
  "workflowAttemptLimit": 10,
  "workflowAttemptWindowMins": 0,
  "imageWritebackRotationIntervalDays": 0,
  "imageWritebackRotationIntervalUnitUi": "string",
  "createdBy": "string",
  "createdAt": 0,
  "updatedAt": 0
}

Field descriptions (response body)

Top-level fields

Field Type Description
id string Verification flow ID assigned by the server. Use this to get or update the flow.
url string URL to access this verification flow directly.
displayName string Display name (max 30 characters).
description string Description (max 255 characters).
status enum ENABLED or DISABLED.
type enum Workflow type: ONBOARDING, RECOVERY, CC_ADMIN, CUSTOM.
frictionLevel enum Friction level: HIGHEST, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW, LOWEST.
steps array List of verification steps generated by the server. Each step has name and optional settings.
approvers array List of approvers generated by the server.
escalationApprovers array List of escalation approvers.
rpAppIdReference string Reference to RP App ID.
codeCustomizations map Map of code customization types to customization IDs.
oidcClientConfigId string OIDC client configuration ID.
escalateToLiveChat boolean Whether escalation to live chat is enabled.
contentCustomizationId string Content customization kit ID.
policyKitId string Policy kit ID reference.
dataRetentionSettings object Data retention settings for document biometric data.
dataRetentionSettings.documentBiometricPolicy enum Retention policy: ONE_DAY, SEVEN_DAYS.
blockDurationMins long Block duration in minutes.
workflowAttemptLimit integer Maximum workflow attempt limit.
workflowAttemptWindowMins long Workflow attempt window in minutes.
imageWritebackRotationIntervalDays integer Image writeback rotation interval in days.
imageWritebackRotationIntervalUnitUi string Unit label for the image writeback rotation interval (UI display only).
createdBy string Username of the user who created this flow.
createdAt long Creation timestamp (epoch milliseconds).
updatedAt long Last update timestamp (epoch milliseconds).

Approver fields (items in approvers and escalationApprovers)

Field Type Description
email string Approver email address.
phoneNumber string Approver phone number.
countryCode string Approver country code in Alpha-2 or Alpha-3 format (e.g. "US", "GBR").
approverType enum MANAGER, SOMEONE_ELSE, DYNAMIC, NONE.
oidcClientConfigId string OIDC client configuration ID for approver authentication.
inviteNextApproverAfterMinutes integer Minutes before inviting the next approver.

Verification step names

Value Description
LOGIN_ID Login identifier step
PHONE_OR_EMAIL Phone or email verification step
LOCATION Location verification step
DOCUMENT_BIOMETRIC Document and biometric step
DOCUMENT_LIVENESS Document liveness check step
VERIFIED_CREDENTIAL Verified credential step
CHAT Chat escalation step
ATTESTATION Approver attestation step
OUTCOME Success outcome step

Status codes

Code Description
200 OK. Request succeeded; response body contains the created verification flow.
400 Bad Request. Invalid request body or parameters (e.g. frictionLevel: NONE, displayName too long).

403 Forbidden. Insufficient permissions.
500 Internal Server Error. Unexpected server error.

Notes

Topic Note
Request shape Send only displayName, description, status, type, frictionLevel, and optionally rpAppIdReference. Do not send steps, approvers, or escalationApprovers.
Friction vs no friction This endpoint requires a non-NONE friction level. For flows with no friction, use POST {{baseUrl}}/cc/api/idv/verification.
Limits displayName max 30 characters; description max 255 characters.
Deprecated step Step name IDV is deprecated; responses use DOCUMENT_BIOMETRIC instead.

item.description:
Overview

The Verification Flows API provides endpoints for creating, managing, and configuring identity verification workflows. Verification flows define the sequence of verification steps that users must complete during identity verification processes, such as employee onboarding, account recovery, or access requests.

What are Verification Flows?

Verification flows are configurable workflows that define how identity verification is performed in Affirm. Each flow specifies:

  1. Steps: The verification steps users must complete (e.g., phone verification, document check, location verification)
  2. Step Settings: Configuration for each step (retry limits, failure outcomes, escalation options)
  3. Approvers: Designated approvers who must verify and approve requests
  4. Outcomes: What happens after successful or failed verification
  5. Customizations: Content customization kits, code customizations, policy kits, and styling
  6. Data Retention: How long document biometric data is retained

Common Use Cases

  • Employee Onboarding: Verify new employee identity during onboarding
  • Account Recovery: Verify user identity when recovering access
  • Access Requests: Verify identity for sensitive access requests
  • Compliance Verification: Meet regulatory requirements for identity verification
  • Custom Workflows: Create organization-specific verification processes

Endpoints

Method Endpoint Description
POST {{baseUrl}}/cc/api/idv/verification Create a new verification flow (frictionLevel must be NONE)
POST {{baseUrl}}/cc/api/idv/verification/friction Create a verification flow with a friction level (HIGHEST, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW, LOWEST)
GET {{baseUrl}}/cc/api/idv/verification/{id} Get a single verification flow by ID
GET {{baseUrl}}/cc/api/idv/verification/list List verification flows with pagination and sort options
GET {{baseUrl}}/cc/api/idv/verification Deprecated. List all verification flows (no pagination). Use /list instead.
PATCH {{baseUrl}}/cc/api/idv/verification Update an existing verification flow (include id in body)
DELETE {{baseUrl}}/cc/api/idv/verification/{id} Delete a verification flow by ID (irreversible)

Authentication & Authorization

All endpoints require a Bearer token and one of the following scopes:

Scope Access
scope: hypr:cc:applications (with principal = CC_ADMIN_RPAPP_ID) Full access for Control Center administrators
scope: hypr:affirm:admin Full access to Affirm features
scope: hypr:affirm:writeVerificationFlow Create, update, and delete verification flows
scope: hypr:affirm:readVerificationFlow Read-only (GET single, GET list). Not sufficient for POST, PATCH, DELETE.

Verification Flow Components

Verification Steps

Step Name Description
LOGIN_ID User enters their login identifier
PHONE_OR_EMAIL Phone or email verification via OTP
LOCATION Location verification (IP allow/block lists, distance threshold)
DOCUMENT_BIOMETRIC Document and biometric verification (document authentication, live photo comparison, motion detection, AML/OFAC check, enhanced identity check)
DOCUMENT_LIVENESS Document liveness check (photo or video capture)
VERIFIED_CREDENTIAL Microsoft Entra Verified Credential presentation verification
CHAT Escalation to live chat support
ATTESTATION Approver attestation and approval
OUTCOME Success outcome step
FAILURE_OUTCOME Failure outcome step

Deprecated: IDV — use DOCUMENT_BIOMETRIC.

Step Settings

Each step can be configured with settings. All setting values are strings in requests and responses (booleans as "true"/"false", numbers as strings, IP lists as JSON-encoded string arrays). Unknown setting keys are silently ignored.

See individual endpoint documentation for the full list of settings per step type.

Approvers

  • Approvers: Primary approvers who review requests
  • Escalation approvers: Contacted if regular approvers do not respond
  • Approver fields: email, phoneNumber, countryCode (Alpha-2 or Alpha-3 country code, e.g. "US", "GBR"), approverType (MANAGER, SOMEONE_ELSE, DYNAMIC, NONE), oidcClientConfigId, inviteNextApproverAfterMinutes

Outcomes

Success outcome (OUTCOME_STEP_RESULT):

  • HYPR_DEVICE_MANAGER — Redirect to Device Manager
  • ISSUE_ENTRA_TAP — Issue Microsoft Entra TAP
  • ISSUE_ENTRA_VERIFIABLE_CREDENTIAL — Issue Microsoft Entra Verified Credential
  • REDIRECT — Redirect to custom URL
  • OKTA_PASSWORD_RESET — Initiate Okta password reset
  • DO_NOTHING — Complete without additional action

Failure outcome (FAILURE_OUTCOME_STEP_RESULT):

  • REDIRECT — Redirect to custom URL
  • DO_NOTHING — Complete without additional action

Customizations

Field Description
contentCustomizationId Content customization kit ID (screens, labels, branding)
codeCustomizations Map of code customization type → customization ID
policyKitId Policy kit ID reference
oidcClientConfigId OIDC client configuration ID for the flow
imageWritebackRotationIntervalDays Image writeback rotation interval in days
imageWritebackRotationIntervalUnitUi Unit label for rotation interval (UI display only)

Data Retention

Field Description
dataRetentionSettings.documentBiometricPolicy Retention policy for document biometric data: ONE_DAY or SEVEN_DAYS. Defaults to SEVEN_DAYS if not specified.

Workflow Types

Type Description
ONBOARDING For new employee onboarding
RECOVERY For account recovery scenarios
CC_ADMIN For Control Center admin operations
CUSTOM Custom workflows (default for create)

Friction Levels

Level Description Endpoint
NONE Custom configuration; you define steps and approvers POST /verification
HIGHEST Maximum security, server-generated steps/approvers POST /verification/friction
HIGH High security POST /verification/friction
MEDIUM Balanced POST /verification/friction
LOW Lower security POST /verification/friction
LOWEST Minimal security POST /verification/friction

Status Codes

Code Description
200 OK. Request succeeded; response body contains the resource (flow or list).
400 Bad Request. Invalid request body or parameters (POST, PATCH).
401 Unauthorized. Missing or invalid authentication token.
403 Forbidden. Insufficient permissions or missing scope.
404 Not Found. Verification flow ID not found (GET by id, PATCH, DELETE).
500 Internal Server Error. Server-side error; see response body for details.

Error Response Format

Errors use RFC 7807 Problem Details (application/json). Example:

{
  "title": "Verification Flow Problem",
  "detail": "The verification flow with id=999 was not found",
  "status": 404,
  "instance": "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890"
}

Limits

  • displayName: max 30 characters
  • description: max 255 characters
  • List pageSize: min 1, max 50

    "loginId": "string (required)",
    "email": "string (optional)",

Unblocks a single user from any workflow. Use when a user was blocked from retrying verification (e.g. after exceeding attempt limits). Send the user’s loginId and the verificationFlowId in the request body. The response indicates whether the unblock succeeded and a message.

Type: Bearer token

item.description:
Overview

The Single User Workflows API provides endpoints for creating, retrieving, deleting, and unblocking single user workflows.

Definitions

  • Verification flow: A configurable template that defines the sequence of verification steps, approvers, and outcomes (e.g. onboarding, recovery). Verification flows are created and managed via the Verification Flows API. A verification flow has an ID and is reusable for many users.

  • Verification request: The act of initiating identity verification for a specific user, or the resulting instance. When you create a verification request, you choose a verification flow and supply the user's identity data (e.g. loginId, email); the system creates a single user workflow for that user.

  • Single user workflow: One user's instance of a verification flow. It is the object created by a verification request: it links one user (via userPii) to one verification flow (verificationFlowId) and has its own id, href, workflowId, and expiresOn. The href is the link you send to the user to start verification.

What are single user workflows?

A single user workflow:

  1. Links a user to a verification flow: Created for a given verificationFlowId and identifies the user via userPii (e.g. loginId, email, name, phone).
  2. Produces a workflow ID and href: After creation, the API returns an id and a href (URL) to send to the user to start verification.
  3. Can be read or deleted by that ID.
  4. Can be unblocked: If a user is blocked from retrying verification (e.g. after too many failures), the unblock endpoint clears the block.

Common Use Cases

  • Programmatic onboarding: Create single user workflows for new employees and send them the verification link.
  • Account recovery: Create a single user workflow for a user who needs to verify identity to recover access.
  • Inspecting or cleaning up: Get a single user workflow by ID or delete it when no longer needed.
  • Unblocking users: Allow a user to retry verification after being blocked.

Endpoints

Method Endpoint Description
POST {{baseUrl}}/cc/api/idv/user Create a new single user workflow
GET {{baseUrl}}/cc/api/idv/user/{id} Get a single user workflow by ID
DELETE {{baseUrl}}/cc/api/idv/user/{id} Delete a single user workflow by ID
POST {{baseUrl}}/cc/api/idv/user/unblock Unblock a single user for a verification flow

Authentication & Authorization

All endpoints require a Bearer token and one of the following scopes:

Scope Access
scope: hypr:cc:applications (with principal = CC_ADMIN_RPAPP_ID) Full access for Affirm administrators
scope: hypr:affirm:admin Full access to Affirm features
scope: hypr:affirm:writeUserFlow Create, delete, unblock; also allows GET by id
scope: hypr:affirm:readUserFlow Read-only (GET by id). Not sufficient for POST create, DELETE, or POST unblock.

Single user workflow structure

Request body (create)

  • verificationFlowId (required): ID of the verification flow to use.
  • userPii (required): User data. loginId is required. All other fields are optional. PII is stored encrypted at rest.
  • redirectUrl, failureRedirectUrl: Optional URLs for dynamic redirect flows.
  • expiresOn: Optional expiration (ISO-8601). If omitted, server applies a default.
  • approvers, escalationApprovers: Optional overrides.
  • steps: Optional step-level overrides (e.g. phoneEmail.failureRedirectUrl).
  • initiatedBy: Optional identifier of the user or system initiating the request.
  • workflowRequestSource: Optional source identifier for the request.

userPii fields

Field Type Required Description
loginId string Yes User's login identifier.
email string No User's email address.
firstName string No First name.
lastName string No Last name.
dateOfBirth string No Date of birth in MM-DD-YYYY format (e.g. "01-31-1990").
phoneNumber string No Phone number.
buildingNumber string No Building or apartment number.
streetAddress string No Street address.
city string No City.
state string No State or region.
postalCode string No Postal code.
countryCode string No Country code.

Approver fields (items in approvers and escalationApprovers)

Field Type Description
email string Approver email address.
phoneNumber string Approver phone number.
countryCode string Approver country code in Alpha-2 or Alpha-3 format (e.g. "US", "GBR").
approverType enum MANAGER, SOMEONE_ELSE, DYNAMIC, NONE. Default: SOMEONE_ELSE.
oidcClientConfigId string OIDC client configuration ID for approver authentication.
inviteNextApproverAfterMinutes integer Minutes before inviting next approver. Default: 0.

Response (create, get, delete)

  • id: Workflow/request ID (use in GET and DELETE path).
  • href: URL to send the user to start verification.
  • userId, workflowId, verificationFlowId, expiresOn.
  • userPii: User data as stored (PII is encrypted at rest).
  • approvers, escalationApprovers: Resolved approvers.
  • redirectUrl, failureRedirectUrl, steps, initiatedBy, workflowRequestSource as applicable.

Unblock request body

  • loginId (required): User's login identifier.
  • verificationFlowId (required): Verification flow ID (numeric long).

Unblock response

  • successful: true if the user was unblocked, false otherwise.
  • message: Human-readable result.

Status Codes

Code Description
200 OK. Request succeeded; response body contains the resource or unblock result.
400 Bad Request. Invalid request body or parameters (e.g. invalid redirectUrl, invalid dateOfBirth format).
401 Unauthorized. Missing or invalid authentication token.
403 Forbidden. Insufficient permissions or missing scope.
404 Not Found. Single user workflow ID or verification flow not found.
500 Internal Server Error. Server-side error; see response body for details.

Error Response Format

Errors use RFC 7807 Problem Details (application/json). Example:

{
  "title": "There was an issue with the single user workflow",
  "detail": "The single user workflow with id=xyz was not found",
  "status": 404,
  "instance": "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890"
}

request.description:
Endpoint

GET {{baseUrl}}/cc/api/idv/workflow/{id}

Returns workflow metadata for the given workflow ID (completion status, result, requestor/approver IDs, and linked user verification request ID).

Authentication

Type: Bearer token

  • Required scope (one of):

    • scope: hypr:cc:applications (with principal = CC_ADMIN_RPAPP_ID)

    • scope: hypr:affirm:admin

    • scope: hypr:affirm:readWorkflow

Request Headers

Header Required Value
Authorization Yes Bearer

Path parameters

Parameter Type Required Description
id string Yes Workflow ID (e.g. from the single user workflow created via the User Verification Requests API).

Response

The response body is a workflow object.

Content-Type: application/json

Response body schema

{
  "id": "string",
  "userVerificationRequestId": "string",
  "isCompleted": false,
  "result": "SUCCESS | FAILURE | NONE",
  "createdOn": "string",
  "requestorUserId": "string",
  "approverUserId": "string"
}

Field descriptions (response body)

Field Type Description
id string Workflow ID.
userVerificationRequestId string The related user verification request ID (from the Single User Workflows API), if applicable. Absent if not created via that API.
isCompleted boolean Whether the workflow has completed.
result enum Outcome: SUCCESS, FAILURE, or NONE. NONE means no attestation yet (workflow not completed).
createdOn string Workflow creation timestamp (ISO-8601 instant).
requestorUserId string Anonymous ID of the requestor (employee).
approverUserId string Anonymous ID of the approver, when applicable and non-automated. Absent when there is no approver.

Result enum values

Value Description
SUCCESS Workflow completed successfully (attestation = success).
FAILURE Workflow completed unsuccessfully (attestation = failure, timeout, or skipped).
NONE No attestation yet — workflow not yet completed.

Status codes

Code Description
200 OK. Request succeeded; response body contains the workflow.
401 Unauthorized. Authentication required.
403 Forbidden. Insufficient permissions.
404 Not Found. No workflow with the given ID.
500 Internal Server Error. Unexpected server error.

Notes

Topic Note
Workflow ID The id in the path is the workflow ID returned when creating a single user workflow (User Verification Requests API).
Result result is derived from attestation: SUCCESS, FAILURE (includes timeout/skipped), or NONE when there is no attestation yet.

item.description:
Overview

The Workflow Management API provides endpoints for querying identity verification workflow instances by ID. It allows you to retrieve workflow metadata (status, completion, result, requestor/approver) and detailed activity results for a given workflow.

Base path: {{baseUrl}}/cc/api/idv/workflow

Definitions

  • Workflow (instance): A single run of an identity verification flow for one user. It has a unique id (workflow ID). Workflows are created via the User Verification Requests API (single user workflows). This API lets you query an existing workflow by that ID.

  • Workflow result: The outcome of a workflow: SUCCESS, FAILURE, or NONE (e.g. not yet completed or no attestation).

What can you do with this API?

  1. Get workflow by ID: Retrieve workflow metadata (id, completion status, result, requestor/approver IDs, linked user verification request ID).

  2. Get workflow results: Retrieve detailed activity log details for a workflow (step statuses, locations, approver decision, etc.).

Common Use Cases

  • Status checks: Determine whether a workflow is completed and whether the result was success or failure.

  • Audit and reporting: Fetch detailed results (e.g. step outcomes, locations, approver notes) for a specific workflow.

  • Linking to user requests: Use the returned userVerificationRequestId to correlate with the User Verification Requests API.

Endpoints

Method Endpoint Description
GET {{baseUrl}}/cc/api/idv/workflow/{id} Get workflow metadata by workflow ID
GET {{baseUrl}}/cc/api/idv/workflow/{id}/results Get detailed activity/results for a workflow by ID

Get workflow by ID

GET {{baseUrl}}/cc/api/idv/workflow/{id}

Returns a summary of one workflow instance by its workflow ID. Use this when you need to know whether a workflow is completed, its outcome (success, failure, or none), when it was created, who the requestor and approver are (by anonymous ID), and the associated user verification request ID if any. The path parameter id is the workflow ID (the same value as workflowId returned when you create a single user workflow via the User Verification Requests API). The response includes id, userVerificationRequestId, isCompleted, result (SUCCESS, FAILURE, or NONE), createdOn, requestorUserId, and approverUserId. Typical use: dashboards, status checks, or looking up the verification request that created this workflow.

Get workflow results

GET {{baseUrl}}/cc/api/idv/workflow/{id}/results

Returns the full activity log details for one workflow. Use this when you need a step-by-step audit of what happened: requester and approver identifiers, workflow type and date, status of each verification step (phone/email, location, identity verification liveness and name check, photo ID and liveness, approver chat/video), the approver’s decision (approved, denied, or not associated), approver notes, IP and browser location data, and optional no-PII aggregated report results. The path parameter id is the same workflow ID as in GET .../workflow/{id}. Typical use: compliance audits, support investigations, and detailed reporting on why a workflow succeeded or failed.

Authentication & Authorization

All endpoints require a Bearer token and one of the following scopes:

Scope Access
scope: hypr:cc:applications (with principal = CC_ADMIN_RPAPP_ID) Full access for Control Center administrators
scope: hypr:affirm:admin Full access to Affirm features
scope: hypr:affirm:readWorkflow Read-only access (GET workflow, GET workflow results).

Domain concepts & enums

Workflow result (result)

Value Description
SUCCESS Workflow completed successfully (attestation = success).
FAILURE Workflow completed unsuccessfully (attestation = failure/timeout/skipped).
NONE No attestation yet (commonly when the workflow is not completed).

Workflow type (workflowType)

Value Description
ONBOARDING Onboarding workflow type.
RECOVERY Account recovery workflow type.
CC_ADMIN Control Center admin workflow type.
CUSTOM Custom workflow type.

Workflow decision (decision)

Value Description
APPROVED Approver approved the workflow.
DENIED Approver denied the workflow.
NOT_ASSOCIATED No approver decision is associated.

Step status (*StepStatus fields)

Value Description
PASS Step passed.
FAILED Step failed.
NOT_CONFIGURED Step is not configured for this workflow.
NOT_ASSOCIATED Step has no data associated (e.g., not run yet).

Location distance unit (location.*.unit)

Value Description
METERS Distance value is in meters.

Workflow metadata structure (GET /{id} response)

Field Type Description
id string Workflow ID.
userVerificationRequestId string Optional. The related user verification request ID, if this workflow was created via the User Verification Requests API.
isCompleted boolean Whether the workflow has completed.
result enum Outcome: SUCCESS, FAILURE, or NONE.
createdOn string Creation time (ISO-8601 instant).
requestorUserId string Anonymous ID of the requestor (employee).
approverUserId string Optional. Anonymous ID of the approver, when applicable and non-automated.

Status codes

Code Description
200 OK. Request succeeded.
401 Unauthorized. Authentication required.
403 Forbidden. Insufficient permissions.
404 Not Found. No workflow with the given ID (or missing {id} path segment).
500 Internal Server Error. Unexpected server error.

Error response format (RFC 7807)

Errors are returned as application/problem+json. Example:

{
  "type": "https://docs.hypr.com/problems/workflow-problem",
  "title": "There was an issue with the workflow",
  "status": 404,
  "detail": "The workflow with id=workflow-instance-abc was not found",
  "instance": "/cc/api/idv/workflow/workflow-instance-abc"
}

request.description:
Endpoint

POST {{baseUrl}}/cc/api/idv/code-customization

Creates a new identity verification code customization.

Authentication

Type: Bearer token

  • Required scope (one of):

    • scope: hypr:cc:applications (with principal = CC_ADMIN_RPAPP_ID)

    • scope: hypr:affirm:admin

    • scope: hypr:affirm:writeCodeCustomization

Request Headers

Header Required Value
Content-Type Yes application/json
Authorization Yes Bearer

Request Body

Content-Type: application/json

Request body is a CodeCustomizationRequest.

Request body schema

{
  "displayName": "string",
  "description": "string",
  "type": "string",
  "content": "string",
  "attributes": {}
}

Field descriptions

Field Type Required Description
displayName string Yes Display name for the code customization.
description string No Optional description.
type enum Yes Code customization type. See type values below.
content string No Code content (base64-encoded script).
attributes object No Map of attribute key to value. Values are stored encrypted. Default: {}.

Type values

Value Description
USER_DIRECTORY_SOURCE Custom user directory lookup by ID.
USER_DIRECTORY_FOR_PHONE_NUMBER_ATTRIBUTE_SOURCE Custom lookup to retrieve phone number attribute from directory.
USER_DIRECTORY_FOR_EMAIL_ATTRIBUTE_SOURCE Custom lookup to retrieve email attribute from directory.
USER_DIRECTORY_FOR_EXTENDED_INFO_ATTRIBUTE_SOURCE Custom lookup to retrieve extended user info attributes from directory.
USER_DIRECTORY_FOR_IMAGE_REPOSITORY_SOURCE Custom lookup to retrieve image from a repository.
USER_DIRECTORY_IMAGE_WRITEBACK Custom logic to write user images back to directory after verification.
SMS_SEND Custom SMS send logic.
SMS_VERIFY Custom SMS verify logic.
EMAIL_SEND Custom email send logic.
OUTCOME_API_CALL Custom API call triggered on verification outcome.

Response

On success the response body is the created code customization (includes the generated id). Attribute values are not returned; only attributes as a list of keys.

Content-Type: application/json

Response body schema

{
  "id": "string",
  "displayName": "string",
  "description": "string",
  "type": "string",
  "content": "string",
  "attributes": ["string"]
}
Field Type Description
id string Code customization ID (numeric string). Use for GET, update, delete, test, and workflow codeCustomizations.
displayName string Display name.
description string Description.
type string Type as stored.
content string Code content as stored.
attributes array of string List of attribute keys (values are not returned).

Status codes

Code Description
200 OK. Request succeeded; response body contains the new code customization with id.
400 Bad Request. Invalid request body (e.g. missing displayName or type).
401 Unauthorized. Authentication required.
403 Forbidden. Insufficient permissions.
500 Internal Server Error. Unexpected server error.

    "content": "<redacted>",
    "attributes": [

}

Endpoint

DELETE {{baseUrl}}/cc/api/idv/code-customization/{id}

Deletes a code customization by ID. The response body is the deleted code customization object. Workflows that referenced this customization are updated (e.g. disabled or reference removed).

Authentication

Type: Bearer token

  • Required scope (one of):

    • scope: hypr:cc:applications (with principal = CC_ADMIN_RPAPP_ID)

    • scope: hypr:affirm:admin

    • scope: hypr:affirm:writeCodeCustomization

Request Headers

Header Required Value
Authorization Yes Bearer

Path parameters

Parameter Type Required Description
id string Yes Code customization ID (numeric string) to delete.

Response

The response body is the deleted code customization object (same structure as returned by GET by ID).

Content-Type: application/json

Response body schema

{
  "id": "string",
  "displayName": "string",
  "description": "string",
  "type": "string",
  "content": "string",
  "attributes": ["string"]
}

Field descriptions (top-level)

Field Type Description
id string Code customization ID.
displayName string Display name.
description string Description.
type enum One of: USER_DIRECTORY_SOURCE, USER_DIRECTORY_FOR_PHONE_NUMBER_ATTRIBUTE_SOURCE, USER_DIRECTORY_FOR_EMAIL_ATTRIBUTE_SOURCE, USER_DIRECTORY_FOR_EXTENDED_INFO_ATTRIBUTE_SOURCE, USER_DIRECTORY_FOR_IMAGE_REPOSITORY_SOURCE, USER_DIRECTORY_IMAGE_WRITEBACK, SMS_SEND, SMS_VERIFY, EMAIL_SEND, OUTCOME_API_CALL.
content string Code content.
attributes array of string List of attribute keys.

Status codes

Code Description
200 OK. Code customization deleted; response body is the deleted object.
401 Unauthorized. Authentication required.
403 Forbidden. Insufficient permissions.
404 Not Found. No code customization with the given ID, or ID is not a valid numeric string.
500 Internal Server Error. Unexpected server error.

Notes

  • Deletion is permanent. Any verification flow that referenced this code customization will have that reference removed or the flow disabled.
  • Use a valid numeric code customization ID. Invalid or non-numeric IDs result in 404 with an RFC 7807 problem detail body.

item.description:
Overview

The Code Customization API provides endpoints for creating, reading, updating, deleting, and testing identity verification (IDV) code customizations. Code customizations are executable logic (e.g. user directory lookups, SMS/email send/verify, outcome API calls) that can be attached to verification flows via workflow configuration codeCustomizations.

Base path: {{baseUrl}}/cc/api/idv/code-customization

What are Code Customizations?

A code customization includes:

  1. displayName – Name for the customization (e.g. for admin UI)
  2. description – Optional description
  3. type – The type of logic this customization performs (see type values below)
  4. content – Code content (base64-encoded script)
  5. attributes – Key-value map of encrypted attributes used by the code at runtime

Common Use Cases

  • User directory – Custom logic to resolve users from a directory (by ID, phone, email, extended info, or image repository), or to write images back after verification
  • SMS / Email – Custom send and verify logic for OTP or notifications
  • Outcome – Custom API call when a verification completes
  • Reuse – Attach one code customization to multiple verification flows via workflow codeCustomizations

Endpoints

Method Endpoint Description
GET {{baseUrl}}/cc/api/idv/code-customization List all code customizations
POST {{baseUrl}}/cc/api/idv/code-customization Create a new code customization
GET {{baseUrl}}/cc/api/idv/code-customization/{id} Get a single code customization by ID
DELETE {{baseUrl}}/cc/api/idv/code-customization/{id} Delete a code customization by ID
POST {{baseUrl}}/cc/api/idv/code-customization/update Update an existing code customization
POST {{baseUrl}}/cc/api/idv/code-customization/test Run a code customization with test input

Authentication

All endpoints require a Bearer token. Required scope depends on the operation:

  • Write (POST create, POST update, DELETE): One of scope: hypr:cc:applications (with principal = CC_ADMIN_RPAPP_ID), scope: hypr:affirm:admin, or scope: hypr:affirm:writeCodeCustomization.
  • Read (GET list, GET by id): One of scope: hypr:cc:applications (with principal = CC_ADMIN_RPAPP_ID), scope: hypr:affirm:admin, scope: hypr:affirm:readCodeCustomization, or scope: hypr:affirm:writeCodeCustomization.
  • Test (POST test): One of scope: hypr:cc:applications (with principal = CC_ADMIN_RPAPP_ID), scope: hypr:affirm:admin, scope: hypr:affirm:writeCodeCustomization, or scope: hypr:affirm:testCodeCustomization.

Code Customization Type values

Value Description
USER_DIRECTORY_SOURCE Custom user directory lookup by ID.
USER_DIRECTORY_FOR_PHONE_NUMBER_ATTRIBUTE_SOURCE Custom lookup to retrieve phone number attribute from directory.
USER_DIRECTORY_FOR_EMAIL_ATTRIBUTE_SOURCE Custom lookup to retrieve email attribute from directory.
USER_DIRECTORY_FOR_EXTENDED_INFO_ATTRIBUTE_SOURCE Custom lookup to retrieve extended user info attributes from directory.
USER_DIRECTORY_FOR_IMAGE_REPOSITORY_SOURCE Custom lookup to retrieve image from a repository.
USER_DIRECTORY_IMAGE_WRITEBACK Custom logic to write user images back to directory after verification.
SMS_SEND Custom SMS send logic.
SMS_VERIFY Custom SMS verify logic.
EMAIL_SEND Custom email send logic.
OUTCOME_API_CALL Custom API call triggered on verification outcome.

Response and Error Format

  • Success responses use Content-Type: application/json.
  • Errors use Content-Type: application/problem+json (RFC 7807). Typical status codes: 400 (Bad Request), 401 (Unauthorized), 403 (Forbidden), 404 (Not Found), 500 (Internal Server Error).

Related Documentation

  • Verification Flows API overview – Attach code customizations to a flow via codeCustomizations.

    • scope: hypr:affirm:admin

Request Headers

Header Required Value
Content-Type Yes application/json
Authorization Yes Bearer

Request Body

Content-Type: application/json

Request body is a BaseContentCustomizationDTO.

displayName is required and validated by the server.

Request body schema

{
  "displayName": "string",
  "description": "string",
  "contentMap": {},
  "stylePaletteMap": {}
}

Field descriptions

Field Type Required Description
displayName string Yes Display name for the content customization kit. Max length: 100.
description string No Optional description. Max length: 255.
contentMap object No Per-screen copy and labels. Omit or send {} for defaults. See contentMap below.
stylePaletteMap object No Theming (colors, sizes, borders). Omit or send {} for defaults. See stylePaletteMap below.

stylePaletteMap (style / theme)

stylePaletteMap controls the visual theme of the IDV flow: header, logo, typography, progress bar, buttons, inputs, and video area. All keys are optional; omitted keys fall back to defaults. Values are typically CSS-friendly strings (e.g. hex colors like #ffffff, sizes like 16px, 1rem).

Progress bar

Key Type Description

Primary button (main CTAs)

Key Type Description
primaryButtonBackgroundColor string Background color.
primaryButtonTextColor string Text color.
primaryButtonHoverBackgroundColor string Background on hover.
primaryButtonFocusBackgroundColor string Background when focused.
primaryButtonBorder string Border (e.g. 1px solid).
primaryButtonBorderColor string Default border color.
primaryButtonHoverBorderColor string Border color on hover.
primaryButtonFocusBorderColor string Border color when focused.
primaryButtonBorderRadius string Border radius (e.g. 4px).
primaryButtonDisabledBackgroundColor string Background when disabled.
primaryButtonDisabledTextColor string Text color when disabled.
primaryButtonDisabledBorderColor string Border color when disabled.

Secondary button

Key Type Description
secondaryButtonBackgroundColor string Background color.
secondaryButtonTextColor string Text color.
secondaryButtonHoverBackgroundColor string Background on hover.
secondaryButtonFocusBackgroundColor string Background when focused.
secondaryButtonBorder string Border.
secondaryButtonBorderColor string Default border color.
secondaryButtonHoverBorderColor string Border color on hover.
secondaryButtonFocusBorderColor string Border color when focused.
secondaryButtonBorderRadius string Border radius.
secondaryButtonDisabledBackgroundColor string Background when disabled.
secondaryButtonDisabledTextColor string Text color when disabled.
secondaryButtonDisabledBorderColor string Border color when disabled.

Tertiary button

Key Type Description
tertiaryButtonBackgroundColor string Background color.
tertiaryButtonTextColor string Text color.
tertiaryButtonHoverBackgroundColor string Background on hover.
tertiaryButtonFocusBackgroundColor string Background when focused.
tertiaryButtonBorder string Border.
tertiaryButtonBorderColor string Default border color.
tertiaryButtonHoverBorderColor string Border color on hover.
tertiaryButtonFocusBorderColor string Border color when focused.
tertiaryButtonBorderRadius string Border radius.

tertiaryButtonDisabledBorderColor string Border color when disabled.

Input fields

Key Type Description

inputContentColor string Input text color.
inputBorderColor string Input border color.

Video area (e.g. document upload / instructions video)

Key Type Description
videoLogoWidth string Logo width in the video section.
videoHeadingContentColor string Heading color in the video section.
videoHeadingContentSize string Heading font size in the video section.

The server uses stylePaletteMap to generate a CSS stylesheet (e.g. via the stylesheet endpoint). Only keys you override need to be present; the rest use default theme values.

contentMap (per-screen copy and labels)

contentMap holds copy and labels for each IDV screen. It is an object whose keys are screen names; each screen key maps to a screen content object. All keys are optional; only screens you customize need entries.

Screen keys in contentMap

Key Description
instructionsScreen Initial instructions and step labels (e.g. verify phone, verify location, verify ID).
consentScreen Consent screen text and loading placeholder.
loginIdentifierScreen Login identifier step: title, description, placeholders, button labels, error messages.
phoneNumberOrEmailScreen Phone/email verification: titles and descriptions for phone vs email vs both, placeholders, hints, OTP disclaimers, error messages.
otpScreen OTP entry: button labels (continue, verify, resend), error messages (code not sent, mismatch, invalid), success messages.
locationScreen Location verification: button labels, error messages, success messages, screen-specific copy.
verifiedCredentialScreen Verified credential step: card header/footer, button labels, error messages, screen-specific content.
idv1Screen IDV1 document/biometric step: titles, descriptions, button labels, error messages.
idv1AwaitScreen IDV1 await/processing screen.
idv1ReportScreen IDV1 report/result screen.
documentUploadVideoScreen Document upload video: button labels, error messages, screen-specific content.
awaitScreen Generic await/processing screen.
approverPreVerifyScreen Approver pre-verification screen.
approverAttestScreen Approver attestation: button labels and screen-specific content.
approverAttestationResultsScreen Approver attestation results.

Structure of each screen object

Each screen value is an object that can contain:

Key Type Description
cardHeader object title, description – shown at the top of the card.
cardFooter object caption1, caption2 – optional footer captions.
buttonLabels object Screen-specific button text (e.g. continueButton, verifyButton, resendButton where applicable).
errorMessages object Screen-specific error messages (e.g. unknown, invalidPhoneNumber, codeMismatchTitle). Keys vary by screen.
successMessages object Screen-specific success messages (e.g. on OTP or location screens). Optional; not all screens have it.
fieldRelatedContent object Placeholders and labels tied to form fields (e.g. loginIdentifierPlaceholder, phoneNumberPlaceholder). Optional.
screenSpecificContent object Extra copy specific to that screen (e.g. step labels on instructions, verification titles on phone/email). Keys vary by screen.

Example: contentMap.instructionsScreen can have cardHeader (title, description), buttonLabels.continueButton, errorMessages (e.g. fetchInstructionsFailed, loadingInstructionsError), and screenSpecificContent with keys like verifyPhoneStepLabel, verifyLocationStepLabel, verifyIdDocumentationStepLabel, loadingPlaceholder. Other screens follow the same pattern with their own button, error, and screen-specific keys. Omitted screens or omitted keys within a screen use server defaults. String values may be sanitized (e.g. XSS) when stored.

Response

On success the response body is the created content customization (ContentCustomizationDTO), including the generated id.

Content-Type: application/json

Response body schema

{
  "id": "string",
  "displayName": "string",
  "description": "string",
  "contentMap": {},
  "stylePaletteMap": {}
}
Field Type Description
id string Content customization ID (numeric string). Use for PATCH, GET by ID, DELETE, and for contentCustomizationId on verification flows.
displayName string Display name.
description string Description.
contentMap object Content map as stored; structure as in contentMap above.
stylePaletteMap object Style palette as stored; structure as in stylePaletteMap above.

Status codes

Code Description
201 Created. Request succeeded; response body contains the new content customization with id.
400 Bad Request. Invalid request body.
401 Unauthorized. Authentication required.
403 Forbidden. Insufficient permissions.
500 Internal Server Error. Unexpected server error.

Notes

  • Content and style values may be sanitized (e.g. XSS) before storage.

  • Use GET {{baseUrl}}/cc/api/idv/content-customization/defaults to obtain a default kit to use as a template.

    • scope: hypr:affirm:admin

    • scope: hypr:affirm:readContentCustomization

    • scope: hypr:affirm:writeContentCustomization

Request Headers

Header Required Value
Authorization Yes Bearer

Path parameters

Parameter Type Required Description
contentCustomizationId string Yes Content customization ID (numeric string).

Response

The response body is a single ContentCustomizationDTO object.

Content-Type: application/json

{
  "id": "string",

Field descriptions (top-level)

Field Type Description

contentMap object Per-screen copy and labels. See contentMap below.

stylePaletteMap (style / theme)

stylePaletteMap controls the visual theme of the IDV flow: header, logo, typography, progress bar, buttons, inputs, and video area. All keys are optional; omitted keys fall back to defaults. Values are typically CSS-friendly strings (e.g. hex colors like #ffffff, sizes like 16px, 1rem).

Key Description

locationScreen Location verification: button labels, error messages, success messages, screen-specific copy.
verifiedCredentialScreen Verified credential step: card header/footer, button labels, error messages, screen-specific content.
idv1Screen IDV1 document/biometric step: titles, descriptions, button labels, error messages.
idv1AwaitScreen IDV1 await/processing screen.
idv1ReportScreen IDV1 report/result screen.
documentUploadVideoScreen Document upload video: button labels, error messages, screen-specific content.
awaitScreen Generic await/processing screen.
approverPreVerifyScreen Approver pre-verification screen.
approverAttestScreen Approver attestation: button labels and screen-specific content.
approverAttestationResultsScreen Approver attestation results.

Structure of each screen object

Each screen value is an object that can contain:

Key Type Description
cardHeader object title, description – shown at the top of the card.
cardFooter object caption1, caption2 – optional footer captions.
buttonLabels object Screen-specific button text (e.g. continueButton, verifyButton, resendButton where applicable).
errorMessages object Screen-specific error messages (e.g. unknown, invalidPhoneNumber, codeMismatchTitle). Keys vary by screen.
successMessages object Screen-specific success messages (e.g. on OTP or location screens). Optional; not all screens have it.
fieldRelatedContent object Placeholders and labels tied to form fields (e.g. loginIdentifierPlaceholder, phoneNumberPlaceholder). Optional.
screenSpecificContent object Extra copy specific to that screen (e.g. step labels on instructions, verification titles on phone/email). Keys vary by screen.

Example: contentMap.instructionsScreen can have cardHeader (title, description), buttonLabels.continueButton, errorMessages (e.g. fetchInstructionsFailed, loadingInstructionsError), and screenSpecificContent with keys like verifyPhoneStepLabel, verifyLocationStepLabel, verifyIdDocumentationStepLabel, loadingPlaceholder. Other screens follow the same pattern with their own button, error, and screen-specific keys. Omitted screens or omitted keys within a screen use server defaults. String values may be sanitized (e.g. XSS) when stored.

Status codes

Code Description
200 OK. Request succeeded; response body contains the content customization.
401 Unauthorized. Authentication required.
403 Forbidden. Insufficient permissions.
404 Not Found. No content customization with the given ID, or ID is not a valid numeric string.
500 Internal Server Error. Unexpected server error.

  • contentCustomizationId must be a valid numeric ID (e.g. as returned from POST create or GET list).

loginIdentifierScreen Login identifier step: title, description, placeholders, button labels, error messages.
phoneNumberOrEmailScreen Phone/email verification: titles and descriptions for phone vs email vs both, placeholders, hints, OTP disclaimers, error messages.
otpScreen OTP entry: button labels (continue, verify, resend), error messages (code not sent, mismatch, invalid), success messages.
locationScreen Location verification: button labels, error messages, success messages, screen-specific copy.
verifiedCredentialScreen Verified credential step: card header/footer, button labels, error messages, screen-specific content.
idv1Screen IDV1 document/biometric step: titles, descriptions, button labels, error messages.
idv1AwaitScreen IDV1 await/processing screen.
idv1ReportScreen IDV1 report/result screen.
documentUploadVideoScreen Document upload video: button labels, error messages, screen-specific content.
awaitScreen Generic await/processing screen.
approverPreVerifyScreen Approver pre-verification screen.
approverAttestScreen Approver attestation: button labels and screen-specific content.
approverAttestationResultsScreen Approver attestation results.

Structure of each screen object

Each screen value is an object that can contain:

Key Type Description
cardHeader object title, description – shown at the top of the card.
cardFooter object caption1, caption2 – optional footer captions.
buttonLabels object Screen-specific button text (e.g. continueButton, verifyButton, resendButton where applicable).
errorMessages object Screen-specific error messages (e.g. unknown, invalidPhoneNumber, codeMismatchTitle). Keys vary by screen.
successMessages object Screen-specific success messages (e.g. on OTP or location screens). Optional; not all screens have it.
fieldRelatedContent object Placeholders and labels tied to form fields (e.g. loginIdentifierPlaceholder, phoneNumberPlaceholder). Optional.
screenSpecificContent object Extra copy specific to that screen (e.g. step labels on instructions, verification titles on phone/email). Keys vary by screen.

Example: contentMap.instructionsScreen can have cardHeader (title, description), buttonLabels.continueButton, errorMessages (e.g. fetchInstructionsFailed, loadingInstructionsError), and screenSpecificContent with keys like verifyPhoneStepLabel, verifyLocationStepLabel, verifyIdDocumentationStepLabel, loadingPlaceholder. Other screens follow the same pattern with their own button, error, and screen-specific keys. Omitted screens or omitted keys within a screen use server defaults. String values may be sanitized (e.g. XSS) when stored.

Status codes

Code Description
200 OK. Response body is the array of content customizations.
401 Unauthorized. Authentication required.
403 Forbidden. Insufficient permissions.
500 Internal Server Error. Unexpected server error.
