item.name: Audit Trail

request.description:
Retrieves a paginated list of Audit Trail Events for an individual RP Application over the specified date range.

The Bearer Token determines the affected RP application; this may be the controlCenterAdmin token.

Added in HYPR version 6.2.0.

Status Codes

200 OK

Path Parameters

rpAppId (string)
The RP Application ID.

startTSUTC (datetime)
The UTC start date/time for the search in Unix Epoch timestamp format (milliseconds).

endTSUTC (datetime)
The UTC end date/time for the search in Unix Epoch timestamp format (milliseconds).

term (string)
An optional filter parameter. The string you specify will be matched against the values for fidoUser, machineUserName, machineId, sessionId, deviceId, and traceId, and the output filtered to just those Audit Trail Events.

Although you can only specify one term parameter per API call, the string is matched across all the fields listed above. If you omit the term parameter or pass an empty value (&term=), all events are included in the results.

pageSize (integer)
The number of events to include on each page in the result set. Default is 20.

pageNumber (integer)
The number of the page you want to return from the paginated set of events. You can only get one page per request and by default the first page is returned.

orderBy (string)
The Audit Trail Event Object property by which to sort the output. By default this is eventTimeInUTC.

sortDir (string)
The sort order for the results. This is descending by default.
[ ASC | DESC ]

Response Body

{
  "data": [
    "<string>"
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "<string>"
  }
}

The response is a single page from the paginated list of Audit Trail Event Objects returned by the search, along with associated response metadata.

data
An array of Audit Trail Event Objects. Each Event Object is the result of a Successful or Failed attempt. See Audit Trail Event Object below.

metadata
Informational data related to the response, for example, total page count, page number, etc. See Audit Trail Response Metadata below.

Each Audit Trail Event Object contains information pertaining to one Event. data in the Response Body is an array of these Event Objects. Each Event Object consists of the following:

id
A unique identifier for this Event.

version
The version of the API.

type
This is currently always AUDIT.

eventName
The name of the event. This may be a Registration Event (e.g., OOB_WEBSITE_REG, OOB_DEVICE_REG), a Website Authentication Event (e.g., OOB_WEBSITE_AUTH, FIDO_ONLY_AUTH), a Workstation Authentication Event (e.g., WORKSTATION_AUTH, WORKSTATION_AUTH_COMPLETE), or some other Event such as Magic Link Created or Mobile Initiated Website Delete. Full documentation for all possible Events can be found under Event Descriptions.

message
A message giving a brief recount of the Event.

subName
The name of the sub-Event. An Event might be broken into multiple steps. The sub-Event distinguishes the various steps. Typically, this is the URI of the request.

eventLoggedBy
The component which logged the Event: [ BROWSER | CONTROL_CENTER_SERVER | ENROLLMENT_SERVICE | MOBILE_DEVICE | RELYING_PARTY_SERVER | UAF_SERVER | WEB | WORKSTATION ]. Success Events are typically logged by the server and failure Events are sent by the mobile device or workstation.

eventTimeInUTC
The UTC time that the Event occurred in Unix Epoch timestamp format.

loggedTimeInUTC
The UTC time that the Event was logged in Unix Epoch timestamp format.

tenantId
The ID of the customer tenant on the HYPR platform.

remoteIP
The IP address of the device which logged the Event.

userAgent
The device User-Agent header from the HTTP request.

traceId
This is a unique identifier that is shared by a series of related Events. This can be passed into a future search in the term parameter.

additionalDetails
A dictionary of content information that is associated with every Audit Trail Event Object. This will vary based on the Event. Depending on the Event, items in additionalDetails may or may not be present in the response, or if present, may not be assigned a value.

  • mobileDevice:

    • os: The device operating system. [ Android | iOS ]

    • osVersion: The operating system version.

    • model: The device model.

    • sdkVersion: The HYPR SDK version.

    • offlineMode:

      • offlineAccessEnabled: Is Offline Mode available to this device? [ true | false ]

      • offlineTokenLength: The number of characters in the offline token.

      • offlineTokenCount: The number of tokens issued.

      • offlineAccessDays: The number of days before the current token expires.

      • tokensAvailable: The number of tokens that have been made avialable to this device.

      • tokensRemaining: The number of unused tokens remaining.

      • extras: Any axtra information.

  • workstation:

    • extendedMessage: Additional context to add to the message.

    • os: The workstation operating system: [ macOS | Windows ]

    • osVersion: The operating system version.

    • model: The workstation model.

    • offlineMode:

      • offlineAccessEnabled: Is Offline Mode available to this workstation? [ true | false ]

      • offlineTokenLength: The number of characters in the offline token.

      • offlineTokenCount: The number of tokens issued.

      • offlineAccessDays: The number of days before the current token expires.

      • tokensAvailable: The number of tokens that have been made avialable to this workstation.

      • tokensRemaining: The number of unused tokens remaining.

  • web:

    • extendedMessage: Additional context to add to the message.

    • machineName: the name of the machine using the web login.

  • smartKey:

    • deviceName: The name of the smart key; e.g., Yubikey 5 NFC.

    • serialNumber: The series identifier of the smart key.

    • firmware: The smart key's firmware version.

    • model: The smart key model.

  • magicLink:

    • createdBy: The user who created the link.

    • createdFor: The user for whom the link was created.

    • validitySeconds: Time in seconds the link will remain valid. Defaults to 86400.

    • authTokenName: The name of the authorization token.

  • featureFlag:

    • featureName: The name of the affected feature flag.

    • editedBy: The username who made the change.

    • newState: [ true | false ]

    • previousState: [ true | false ]

  • createUser: Information about the new user.

  • deleteUser:

    • fullname: The entire name of the deleted user.

  • fido2Setting:

    • setting: The URL of the FIDO2 RP application server.

  • metadataCertExpiry:

    • aaid: The authenticator attestation ideintifier using the certificate.

    • remainingDays: The number of days left before the certificate expires.

    • criticality: The urgency of the expiration. [ LOW | MEDIUM | HIGH ]

  • deviceSignal:

    • signalsBeingSaved: Signal type; one of: [ DEVICE | LOCATION | NETWORK ].

    • signalDeviceId: A unique identifier of the device associated with this signal.

  • desktopSSO:

    • rpAppId: See below.

    • machineUserName: See below.

    • hmac: The HMAC key.

  • deregistration:

    • initiatedBy: The initiating component: [ MOBILE | BROWSER | DEVICE ].

    • deletedRegistration: The deleted component: [ MOBILE | BROWSER | DEVICE ].

    • isLastRegisteredDevice: Is this the last registered device? [ true | false ]

  • logsSubmission: Is this Event a submission of log data? [ true | false ]

  • recoveryPinRetrieval:

    • pinRetrievedBy: The username requesting PIN retrieval.

  • passkey:

    • fido2RpId: The FIDO2 relying party identifier.

    • credentialId: The credential identifier.

    • fido2Username: The FIDO2 username registered with the RP.

  • extras: An array of information pertinent to the Event, often specifically in addition to one of the other parameters in additionalDetails.

  • sslPins: A list of SSL PIN hashes (may be redacted).

isSuccessful
Was the event successful?
[ true | false ]

errorCode
An error code to identify specific issue if relevant. See the Error Codes Troubleshooting Table for information on specific errors.

errorSeverity
The severity of the error Event. This will always be populated when isSuccessful is false.
[ WARN | ERROR | FATAL ]

deviceType
The category of the device which logged the Event.
[ MOBILE | SECURITY_KEY | WEBAUTHN ]

rpAppId
The camel case unique RP application identifier.

deviceId
An ID for the mobile device or other hardware device involved in the Event.

machineId
An ID for the entity (web or workstation) involved in the event.

sessionId
The session id associated with the Event.

fidoUser
The FIDO user name associated with this Event.

machineUserName
The user name for the entity (web or workstation) involved in the Event.

authenticator
This is currently unused and returns null.

usageType
This is currently unused and returns null.

integrationType
This is currently unused and returns null.

integrationProvider
This is currently unused and returns null.

wsOS
The OS for the workstation.

deviceOS
The OS for the mobile device or security key.

wsOSVersion
The version number for the workstation OS.

deviceOSVersion
The version number for the mobile device OS. For security keys, this is the firmware version.

wsRelVersion
The version number for the HYPR Workforce Access Client installed on the workstation.

deviceRelVersion
The version number for the HYPR Mobile App installed on the device.

sdkRelVersion
The version number for the HYPR Mobile SDK.

serverRelVersion
The version number for the HYPR Server.

wsModel
The make and model of the workstation hardware.

deviceModel
The make and model of the mobile device hardware.

machineName
The name of the CC server.

machineDomain
The domain to which the machine belongs, if any.

origin
The origin of this request.

Audit Trail Response Metadata

"metadata": {
  "totalRecords": 0,
  "totalPages": 0,
  "pageSize": 0,
  "currentPage": 0
}

The total number of Events in the result set.

The total number of pages in the result set.

pageSize
The number of Events on each page in the result set, as set by the pageSize parameter in the request.

currentPage
The number of this page in the paginated result set.

request.description:
Create a device Event and add it to the HYPR log stream.

The Bearer Token determines the affected RP application; this may be the controlCenterAdmin token.

Added in HYPR 7.0.0.

Status Codes

200 OK

Request Body Parameters

isSuccessful
Was the recorded event a successful attempt?
[ true | false ]

loggedTimeInUTC
The timestamp of the Event logging (vs. when it occurred) in UTC format.

version
The negotiated HYPR version.

type
What type of Event is it? This may have one of several posible value sets:

  • Default: AUDIT

  • DeviceType: [ ANDROID | IOS | SMART_KEY | WEBAUTHN ]

  • MachineType: [ WEB | WORKSATION | WORKSTATION_DOMAIN | VDI ]

eventName
The uppercase name of the Event; EX: CREATE_APP

message
The accompanying message, if any. This can contain any number of secondary values.

subName
Most often this will be the relative path to the endpoint associated with the Event (EX: /rp/deviceapi/audit); it may also be a short description of the action taken, such as PUSH, EMAIL, etc.

eventLoggedBy
The component which logged the Event: [ BROWSER | CONTROL_CENTER_SERVER | ENROLLMENT_SERVICE | MOBILE_DEVICE | RELYING_PARTY_SERVER | UAF_SERVER | WEB | WORKSTATION ]. Success Events are typically logged by the server and failure Events are sent by the mobile device or workstation.

eventTimeInUTC
The timestamp of the Event (vs. when it was logged) in UTC format.

traceId
the HYPR-assigned tracker unique to this Event.

additionalDetails
An array containing subsidiary attributes appropriate to the Event. If attributes do not apply to the Event, they can be omitted or left as null.

  • extras: Extra information not included in the default Event layout, possibly associated with third-party functions.

  • mobileDevice: An data object describing the device's attributes.

    • extras: Extra information not included in the default Event layout, possibly associated with third-party functions.

    • model: The device's model.

    • os: The device's operating system (OS) type.

    • osVersion: The mobile OS version number.

    • sdkVersion: The HYPR SDK version.

    • offlineMode: An array containing attributes governing Offline Mode behaviors.

      • offlineAccessDays: Days a user is allowed to continue offline logins before needing to login to refresh the offline tokens. Default is 30.

      • offlineAccessEnabled: Is offline access enabled? [ true | false ]

      • offlineTokenCount

      • offlineTokenLength: The length of the token in characters. Default is 8.

      • tokensAvailable: The number of offline PINs distributed to a user. Default is 25.

      • tokensRemaining: The number of unused tokens remaining for the user.

  • workstation: An array containing workstation attributes by grouping.

    • keyAgreement: An array holding key comparison information.

      • publicKey: The public key value.

      • publicKeyAuth: The source of the authorization; typically an RP server and browser.

    • login: Login certificate attributes.

      • ivLoginCert: The initialization vector value.

      • loginCert: The login certificate value.

      • loginCertAuth: The authorization code for the certificate.

      • signingCert: The signing certificate value.

    • offline: Offline token management.

      • tokens: An array of avialble tokens.

      • tokensAuth: The authorization code for the token.

    • web: Web-related attributes.

      • extendedMessage: Additional information not carried in the message attribute.

      • machineName: The name of the machine making the web request.

    • smartKey: Attributes for security keys.

      • deviceName: The name of the device.

      • serialNumber: The device serial number.

      • firmware: The device firmware version.

      • model: The device's model.

    • magicLink: Attributes for a magic link.

      • authTokenName: The token's name given at creation.

      • createdBy: The user who created the token.

      • createdFor: The token's recipient.

      • validitySeconds: How many seconds the token will be valid. Default is 86400 (24 hours).

    • featureFlag: Feature flag attributes,

      • featureName: The uppercase name of the feature flag. EX: MOBILE AUTO_CERT_RENEWAL

      • newState: The state to which the feature flag was changed. [ true | false ]

      • previousState: The state from which the feature flag was changed. [ true | false ]

      • editedBy: The user making the change.

    • createUser: Attributes specific to user creation.

      • fullName: The user's entire name as seen in User Management.

      • createdBy: The user creating this user.

      • createdFor: The username for the new user.

    • deleteUser: Attributes specific to user deletion.

      • fullName: The user's entire name as seen in User Management.

    • fido2Setting: Attributes specific to FIDO2 settings.

      • setting: The FIDO client origin URL.

    • metadataCertExpiry: Attributes specific to FIDO metadata certificate expiry.

      • aaid: The authenticator attestation identifier (AAID) involved in this Event.

      • remainingDays: Days left before the certificate expires.

      • criticality: How critical is the need to update.

    • deviceSignal: Attributes specific to device signals.

      • signalsBeingSaved: The type of signals being saved:

        • BLUETOOTH

        • DEVICE

        • LOCATION

        • MOTION

        • NETWORK

        • TELEPHONY

        • WIFI

      • signalDeviceId: The unique identifier for the device generating the signal.

    • desktopSSO: Attributes specific to HYPRspeed.

      • webNamedUserRequested: The web username for the user in question.

      • workstationMachineId: The organization's name for the workstation. EX: GHOPPER-MAC

      • workstationNamedUser: The SSO username for the user in question. EX: ghopper

      • workstationRPAppId: The camel case unique RP application identifier associated with this workstation.

    • deregistration: Attributes specific to user deregistration.

      • initiatedBy: The username who initiated the deregistration attempt.

      • deletedRegistration: The type of registration that was removed: [ BROWSER | MOBILE_DEVICE | WORKSTATION ]

      • isLastRegisteredDevice: Is this the last registered device for this user? If so, appropriate warnings may occur. [ true | false ]

    • logsSubmission: Attributes specific to logs submission.

      • logsId: The specific ideitifier of this logs submission.

    • recoveryPinRetrieval: Attributes specific to recovery PINs.

      • pinRetrievedBy: The username who retrieved the PINs.

errorCode
The HYPR error code, if applicable. See our Error Codes list for full descriptions of errors.

errorSeverity
How bad is it?
[ ERROR | FATAL | WARN ]

deviceType
The type of device creating the Event.
[ ANDROID | IOS | SMART_KEY | WEBAUTHN ]

rpAppId
The camel case unique RP application identifier.

deviceId
The unique identifier for the device.

machineId
The unique identifier for the machine.

sessionId
The unique identifier for the session.

fidoUser
The FIDO username, which may differ from the HYPR username or the machineUserName.

machineUserName
The username for this machine.

authenticator
The authenticator identifier used for this Event. EX: 0045#1040

usageType
Currently not used.

integrationType
Is the integration a standalone implementation, or does it share enrollment with an existing integration?
[ EXISTING | NEW ]

integrationProvider
Uppercase value representing the type of integration. EX: AZURE_AD, ONELOGIN, etc.

deviceOSVersion
The device's OS version.

deviceModel
The device's OS model.

machineDomain
The domain to which the machine belongs.

machineName
The machine name on the network. EX: GHOPPER-WIN

credentialId
A unique identifier for the credential.

Response Body

{
  "status": {
    "responseCode": "",
    "responseMessage": ""
  }
}

status
An array holding response status information

  • responseCode: The HTTP code for the result.

  • responseMessage: The message associated with the responseCode.

item.name: GET all the devices and users in an rpApp by machineDisplayName.

request.description:
Returns all the registered devices to a machine and the specified RP application username.

The Bearer Token determines the affected RP application; this may be the controlCenterAdmin token.

Status Codes

200 OK

Path Parameters

rpAppId (string)
The camel case unique RP application identifier.

machineDisplayName (string)
The name of the machine.

Request Body

The Request Body is empty.

Response Body

The Response Body is identical to that of Get registered devices by MachineName (GET /rp/api/oob/client/devices/:appIdWS/:machineName).

response.name: OK
response.body:
[

item.name: Delete a device from an application user.

request.description:
Remove a device from the specified RP application username.

The Bearer Token determines the affected RP application; this may be the controlCenterAdmin token.

Added in HYPR version 3.8.0.

Status Codes

200 OK

Path Parameters

rpAppId (string)
The camel case unique RP application identifier.

username (string)
the HYPR username.

deviceId (string)
The HYPR-assigned unique device identifier; obtained by using any of the related GET statements.

Request Body

The Request Body is empty.

Response Body

Returns true if successful and false if not.

response.name: OK
response.body: <boolean>

request.description:
Delete a mobile device from the specified RP application.

The Bearer Token determines the affected RP application; this may be the controlCenterAdmin token.

Added in HYPR version 3.8.0.

Status Codes

200 OK

Request Path Parameters

rpAppId (string)
The camel case unique application identifier associated with the device being deleted.

username (string)
The username associated with the device being deleted.

deviceId (string)
The unique identifier of the device being deleted.

Response Body

true

The Response Body contains the value true or false.

response.name: Delete a registered device.
response.body: true

request.description:
Creates a QR authentication request.

The Bearer Token determines the affected RP application; this may be the controlCenterAdmin token.

Status Codes

200 OK

Request Body Parameters

Parameters for this request are identical to those for Send push request to start authentication (POST /rp/api/oob/client/authentication/requests).

Response Body

{
  "dynamicLink": "<string>",
  "landingPage": "<string>",
  "sessionId": "<string>",
  "qrFallbackActivationCode": "<string>"
}

dynamicLink
The link content for use when a user has only a phone and no workstation to scan a QR code.

landingPage
The URL of the landing page; typically http://:/rp/oob/qr/client/landing/:appId, where appId is the camel case unique RP application identifier.

sessionId
The unique identifier for the session.

qrFallbackActivationCode
The multi-caracter code used for cases when QR is not available (broken camera, policy limits, etc.).

response.name: OK
response.body:
{
  "dynamicLink": "<string>",
  "landingPage": "<string>",
  "rpAppId": "<string>",
  "sessionId": "<string>",
  "qrFallbackMobileURL": "<string>",
  "qrFallbackActivationCode": "<string>"
}

request.description:
Initiate an OOB authentication request.

The Bearer Token determines the affected RP application; this may be the controlCenterAdmin token.

Added in HYPR version 3.8.0.

Status Codes

200 OK

Request Body Parameters

appId
The camel case unique RP application identifier.

deviceNonce
The contents of the nonce for this device.

includeQRFallbackCode
Will the user be able to fall back upon manual code entry instead of using a QR scanner?
[ true | false ]

machine
The machine name.

namedUser
The machine username making the request.

serviceHmac
The hashed message authentication code (HMAC) for the service.

serviceNonce
The contents of the nonce for this service.

sessionNonce
The contents of the nonce for this session.

machineId
The HYPR-generated unique machine identifier.

deviceId
The HYPR-generated unique device identifier.

clientType
HYPR label defining the client.
[ WEB | WORKSTATION ]

actionId
The unique identifier for the action as defined in CC Advanced Mode: Policy Management.

additionalDetails
Any additional parameters to help communicate appropriate data.

Response Body

{
  "requestId": "28AD600AD2858F9B270B5AA5801054EE3977937EAD40F8B090D8035E614E4604",
  "links": [
    {
      "rel": "self",
      "href": "http://host-name/rp/oob/client/authentication/requests/28AD600AD2858F9B270B5AA5801054EE3977937EAD40F8B090D8035E614E4604"
    }
  ]
}

requestId
The unique identifier for this push request.

links
An array of link data.

  • rel: the HTML relationship between the link document and this one. See the HTML tag info.
  • href: The URL including the requestId.

response.name: OK

request.description:

  • enabled: Is this flag currently in use? [ true | false ]
  • releaseVersion: The HYPR version when this flag was introduced.
  • deprecatedStatus: Is this flag deprecated? [ true | false ]
  • involvedComponents: A data object containing comma-separated HYPR components. [ SERVER | CLIENT | DEVICE | HAAS ]

rpAppConfig
An array containing RP application configuration data.

  • rpApps: An array containing individual RP application data.
    • rpAppId: The camel case unique RP application identifier.
    • rpAppName: The human-readable name assigned to the RP application when it was created.
    • features: A data object containing RP application feature flag data.
      • name: The name of the flag. Typically written IN_ALL_CAPS.
      • description: The purpose of the flag.
      • enabled: Is this flag currently in use? [ true | false ]
      • releaseVersion: The HYPR version when this flag was introduced.
      • deprecatedStatus: Is this flag deprecated? [ true | false ]
      • involvedComponents: A data object containing comma-separated HYPR components. [ SERVER | CLIENT | DEVICE | HAAS ]

versionControl
A data object for version control rules.

  • platform: The platform for the rule. [ ANDROID | HYPR | IOS ]
  • minVersion: The minimum version number for the platform, expressed as major.minor.patch. EX: 8.12.2
  • effectiveOn: The date the rule goes into effect, in UTC format.

pushConfigs
A data object containing push-related toggles.

  • pushEnabled: Are push notifications enabled for this RP application? [ true | false ]
  • qrEnabled: Is QR Login enabled for this RP application? [ true | false ]
  • workstationSSOEnabled: Is HYPRspeed enabled for this RP application? [ true | false ]

item.name: Browser
Send browser fingerprint data to Control Center.

request.description:
Deliver browser fingerprint data to Control Center. If successful, a BROWSER_SIGNAL_RECEIVED Event is recorded in the Audit Trail.

The Bearer Token determines the affected RP application; this may be the controlCenterAdmin token.

Added in HYPR version 8.7.0.

Status Codes

200 OK
Indicates Success. A standard status code message will be accompanied by a full list of the signals data sent.

400 Bad Request
Check the syntax of the request.

Request Body Parameters

rpAppId
The camel case unique RP Appliction identifier.

deviceId
The unique identifier for the device.

userName
The HYPR username targeted by the request.

data
An array containing signals information.

  • browser: An array containing browser signal data.
    • navigator: An array containing browser navigator data.
      • bluetoothAvailability: Boolean value indicating if Bluetooth is available. [ true | false ]
      • device: The hardware model.
      • deviceMemory: The available memory.
      • hardwareConcurrency: The hardware compatiblity version.
      • maxTouchPoints: If the device uses a touch screen, how many touch points can be used?
      • platform: The specific form factor.
      • system: The operating system brand.
      • userAgentData: More details about the device and browser.
        • architecture: The chipset make.
        • brands: A data object listing browser brand names.
        • mobile: Is this a mobile device? [ true | false ]
        • platform: The operating system.
        • platformVersion: The operating sysem version.
      • vendor: The browser's vendor.
    • screen: Screen-specific browser details.
      • height: The height of the screen in pixels.
      • width The width of the screen in pixels.
      • pixelDepth: The pixel quality expressed in bits.
      • colorDepth: The color quality expressed in bits.
      • lied: Is any screen information suspect? [ true | false ]
    • workerScope: Information specific to the working environment.
      • deviceMemory: MB of hardwrae memory.
      • hardwareConcurrency: The hardware compatiblity version.
      • language: The language being used.
      • platform: The specific form factor.
      • system: The operating system brand.
      • device: The hardware model.
      • timezoneLocation: In which time zone does the signal originate? This field uses standard timezone labels.
      • webglRenderer: The graphics renderer.
      • webglVendor: The graphics renderer vendor.
      • userAgentData: More details about the device and browser.
        • architecture: The chipset make
        • brands: A data object listing browser brand names.
        • mobile: Is this a mobile device? [ true | false ]
        • model: The model of the device.
        • platform: The operating system.
        • platformVersion: The operating sysem version.
    • canvasWebgl: Information about WebGL.
      • gpu: Graphics processor unit data.
        • parts: A comma-separated list of hardware.
        • confidence: An expression of trust for the values returned.
        • grade: A letter grade reflecting the confidence level.
        • compressedGPU: The GPU manufacturing data.
      • timezone
        • locationMeasured: A reflection of the time zone where the signal originates.
        • lied: Is any timezone information suspect? [ true | false ]
      • fonts: A comma-separated list of fonts in use.

Response Body

Successful Response includes a message indicating success, plus a data object containing the entire object or the specified subset. Attributes for the Response Body mirror those of the Request.

        • mobile: Is this a mobile device? [ true | false ]

        • platform: The operating system in use.

        • platformVersion: The operating system version.

      • vendor: The browser vendor.

      • colorDepth: The number of bits for each color component in a pixel.

      • lied: Does the current browser snapshot differ from the stored browser fingerprint? [ true | false ]

The Response may include any of the following components:

      • canvas2d: Canvas 2D information.

      • canvasWebgl: Includes GPU information and supported Webgl extensions.

      • capturedErrors

      • clientRects: The bounding rectangles for each box in a client.

      • consoleErrors

      • css: Including MimeTypes.

      • cssMedia

      • features

      • fonts

      • headless: Detect if browser is operating in a headless mode; i.e. Selenium.

      • htmlElementVersion: Measures HTML element support.

      • intl: International locale information.

      • lies: Does this information differ from the stored fingerprint?

      • maths: Measures support for various math functions.

      • media

      • navigator: See above.

      • offlineAudioContext: Includes audio device information.

      • resistance: Measures privacy functions enabled in Browser or OS.

      • screen: See above.

      • svg: Measures SVG rendering.

      • timezone

      • trash

      • voices: Measures SpeechSynthesis (Text-to-Speech) and SpeechRecognition (Asynchronous Speech Recognition).

      • windowFeatures: Measures supported window features.

      • workerScope: See above.

The time when the signal was generated, in UTC format.

request.description:
Create an application with the minimally required configuration settings.

This call only works using the controlCenterAdmin Bearer Token.

This call is used to create a new RP Application; in Control Center Standard Mode, a new RP application is created for each integration using this call. In Control Center Advanced Mode, in the left navigation menu, clicking Add Application generates this call. See Creating RP Applications in the product documentation.

item.description:
RP Application policies, user management, auditing, and device pair management. Specific features include the following:

  • Single registration

  • Out-of-band registration

  • SSL Pinning

All of the calls herein require the Bearer Token specific to the affected RP Application.

item.name: Workstation
Certificates

request.description:
Add an encrypted certificate to HYPR Passwordless client.

Added in HYPR version 6.18.0.

Status Codes

204 No Content
Indicates success.

Upon failure, a specific error is recorded to the log stream, according to RFC7807. See Response Body, below.

Request Body Parameters

errorCode
A specific error code indicating the issue.

errorMessage
The description of the error.

issuerKeyAgreementPublicKey
The enrollment service's public key; used to derive the environment key.

issuerKeyAgreementPublicKeyAuth
An authorization code for the public key.

ivLoginCert
The identity verification login certificate.

loginCert
The login certificate.

loginCertAuth
An authorization code for the login certificate.

loginCertExpiryDate
The login certificate's end of life date in UTC milliseconds format.

loginCertSerialNumber
The serial production number for the login certificate.

machineUserNameWS
The specific username logged into this machine making the request.

machineUserNames
An array of username values associated with the machine. If more than one is found, all will be listed here in comma-separated format.

requestId
The unique identifier for this request.

signingCert
The signing certificate value.

Response Body

There is no response for success except the Status Code above.

If an error condition occurs, the following JSON is returned:

{
  "errorCode": "<integer>",
  "errorMessage": "<string>",
  "requestId": "<long>"
}

errorCode
The error number associated with the issue.

errorMessage
The description of the error.

requestId
The requestId echoed back from the Request Body.

item.name: List any pending certificate issue and revocation requests.

request.description:
New certificate requests come from new web registration and/or direct certificate renewal.

Revoked certificate serial numbers are from certs which have been de-registered, unenrolled, or renewed.

The Bearer Token must be the controlCenterAdmin token.

Status Codes

200 OK

Request Body

The Request Body is empty.

Response Body

{
  "loginCerts": [
    {
      "deviceId": "<string>",
      "deviceKeyAgreementPublicKey": "<string>",
      "encCounter": "<string>",
      "machineUserName": "<string>",
      "requestId": "<long>",
      "requestTimeoutInSecs": "<long>",
      "machineUserNameWS": "<string>"
    },
    {
      ...
    }
  ],
  "revokedCerts": [
    {
      "certSerialNumber": "<string>",
      "requestId": "<long>",
      "requestTimeoutInSecs": "<long>"
    },
    {
      ...
    }
  ]
}

If the request finds no certificates, loginCerts and revokedCerts will both be empty [ ].

loginCerts
A data object containing current certificate information.

  • requestId: The unique identifier for the certificate request.
  • requestTimeoutInSecs: The number of seconds before the request becomes invalid.
  • machineUserNameWS: The workstation username, including domains or local machine names. EX: HIGHLANDSBANK-ghopper
  • machineUserName: The HYPR username associated with the machine making the request.
  • deviceKeyAgreementPublicKey: The public key.
  • deviceId: The unique device identifier.
  • encCounter: A short string used to strengthen random elements.

revokedCerts
A data object listing revoked certificate information.

  • certSerialNumber: The certificate production order number.
  • requestId: The unique identifier for the request.
  • requestTimeoutInSecs: The number of seconds before the request becomes invalid.

response.name: OK

item.name: Trigger or re-trigger a certificate enrollment.

request.description:
Initiate WS certificate enrollment.

Typically this will happen automatically after a web registration provided the appropriate Single Registration feature is enabled. Contact HYPR Support to enable the correct feature for this flow.

However, if this feature is disabled during registration and you want to register a user after the fact, this endpoint may be used. The assumption is that the Device has an existing corresponding web registration pending.

The Bearer Token must be the controlCenterAdmin token.

Status Codes

204 No Content
Indicates success.

Request Body Parameters

deviceId
The unique device identifier.

machineId
The unique machine identifier.

machineUserName
The account logged into the machine.

machineUserNameWS
A comma-separated list of all possible usernames associated with the machine.

deviceKeyAgreementPublicKey
The contents of the public key.

rpAppId
The camel case unique RP application identifier.

Response Body

There is no response for success except the Status Code above.

If an error condition occurs, the following JSON is returned:

{
  "errorCode": "<integer>",
  "errorMessage": "<string>",
  "requestId": "<long>"
}

errorCode
The error number associated with the issue.

errorMessage
The description of the error.

requestId
The requestId echoed back from the Request Body.

request.description:
The workstation makes this call once the browser initiates SSO to look up the last successful FIDO session it had; then it signs the browser challenge using its signing key from registration.

the unique identifier for the machine.

request.description:
Enables and configures optional HYPR workstation login features.

The Bearer Token determines the affected RP application; this may be the controlCenterAdmin token.

This call governs the toggles described under Workstation Settings in the HYPR Product Documentation.

Added in HYPR version 7.0.0.

200 OK

{
  "loginEnabled": <boolean>,
  "enforcesUserPresence": <boolean>,
  "logsSubmission": <boolean>,
  "smartkeysEnabled": <boolean>,
  "offlineAccess": {
    "enabled": <boolean>,
    "tokenLength": <integer>,

    "tokenEntryTimeoutSecs": <integer>,
    "offlineAccessDays": <integer>,
    "tokenLowWarningThresholdPercentage": <integer>
  },
  "recoveryPins": {
    "enabled": <boolean>,
    "pinLength": <integer>,
    "pinCount": <integer>,
    "pinAccessHours": <integer>
  },
    "smartKeyRecoveryPins": {
    "enabled": <boolean>,
    "pinLength": <integer>,
    "pinCount": <integer>,
    "pinAccessHours": <integer>
  },
  "vdiEnabled": <boolean>,
  "onboardingCompletedMac": <boolean>,
  "onboardingCompletedWindows": <boolean>,
  "advancedModeMac": <boolean>,
  "advancedModeWindows": <boolean>

loginEnabled
If true, enables domain joined users to pair with HYPR. This setting should not be changed following active deployment and enrollment of end users.

enforcesUserPresence
If true, prompts users to enter their workstation account password as an extra security step when registering a mobile device.

logsSubmission
If true, HYPR Mobile App and WFA user logs can be submitted directly to your tenant logs stream. Logs will automatically be forwarded to the HYPR Support Team to assist with troubleshooting.

smartkeysEnabled
If true, allows users to register a smart key via the HYPR Workforce Access Client and use it for workstation authentication as an alternative to their mobile device.

offlineAccess
A collection of settings to allow users to perform a PIN-based login when they don’t have an internet connection for either their mobile device or the workstation itself.

  • enabled: If true, enables a user to login to their workstation without Internet access.
  • tokenLength: The number of alphanumeric characters users must enter on the workstation login screen when their mobile device or the workstation is offline (6-13). Defaults to 8.
  • tokenCount: The number of times a user can access their machine while offline (10-25). When the limit is reached, the user must perform an online login to restart the count. Defaults to 25. Users are warned when they have 20% of their count remaining.
  • tokenEntryTimeoutSecs: The number of seconds to display the PIN on the user's smartphone (30-300). Defaults to 180 seconds.
  • offlineAccessDays: The number of consecutive days a user can log in while offline (7-90). When the limit is reached, the user must perform an online login to restart the count in order to continue to log in while offline. Defaults to 30 days. This parameter works in conjunction with the tokenLowWarningThresholdPercentage parameter.
  • offlinePINPromptSecs: The number of seconds the application waits until displaying the offline PIN prompt during an online authentication attempt. Defaults to 5 seconds.
  • tokenLowWarningThresholdPercentage: The threshold at which to warn the user that they are running low on offline access days. Defaults to 20%. For example, if tokenLowWarningThresholdPercentage is set to 20 and offlineAccessDays is set to 90, the user is warned when they have 18 days left.

recoveryPins
A collection of settings to allow users to perform a PIN-based login when they don’t have access to their mobile device.

  • enabled: If true, enables users to perform a PIN-based login when they don’t have access to their mobile device.
  • pinLength: The number of alphanumeric characters users need to enter on the workstation login screen when they request a Recovery PIN (6-13).
  • pinCount: The number of Recovery PINs generated during the pairing process (1-10).
  • pinAccessHours: The number of hours for which the Recovery PIN is valid (24-72). The timer starts when the user first logs into the workstation using the PIN.

vdiEnabled
(Windows Only) If true, allows users to pair their mobile device once and then access any domain-joined desktop by scanning a QR code displayed on the login screen.
[ true | false ]

onboardingCompletedMac
For HYPR internal use only.

onboardingCompletedWindows
For HYPR internal use only.

advancedModeMac
For HYPR internal use only.

advancedModeWindows
For HYPR internal use only.

smartKeyRecoveryPins
A collection of settings to allow security key users to perform a PIN-based login when they don’t have access to their security key.

  • enabled: If true, enables users to perform a PIN-based login when they don’t have access to their security key. [ true | false ]
  • pinLength: The number of alphanumeric characters users need to enter on the workstation login screen when they request a Security Key Recovery PIN (6-13).
  • pinCount: The number of security key recovery PINs generated during the pairing process (1-10).
  • pinAccessHours: The number of hours for which the security key recovery PIN is valid (24-72). The timer starts when the user first logs into the workstation using the PIN.

Response Body

The response echoes back the Request Body parameters.

item.name: Magic Links

request.description:
Create a Magic Link. The payload returned will include both a web link (webLink) and a dynamic link (firebaseDynamicLinkForHyprApp). You can then communicate either the web link or dynamic link to the user you want to register.

The dynamic link, firebaseDynamicLinkForHyprApp is generated using Firebase dynamic links.

You will also notice a mobileDeepLink returned in the response. This is the registration link to the Control Center instance which will be the destination of your dynamic link.

The Bearer Token determines the affected RP application; this may be the controlCenterAdmin token.

Added in HYPR 6.6.0.

Status Codes

200 OK

Request Body Parameters

appId
The camel case unique RP application identifier.

action
In the case of a dynamic link, this will append an action query parameter to the dynamic link. This will tell the HYPR Mobile App that is parsing the dynamic link whether the dynamic link is for authentication or registration. When using the HYPR Mobile App, this should be either AUTH or REG.

username
Enter the name of the user for whom you want to generate the Magic Link.

  • Note: If you’re using HYPR with Okta, Ping Identity, ForgeRock, or another SSO provider, make sure the user already exists in that system.

email
This information will be stored with the Magic Link and available in the response from Retrieve a Magic Link (/rp/api/versioned/magiclink?token=:magicLinkToken).

firstname
This information will be stored with the Magic Link and available in the response from Retrieve a Magic Link (/rp/api/versioned/magiclink?token=:magicLinkToken).

lastname
This information will be stored with the Magic Link and available in the response from Retrieve a Magic Link (/rp/api/versioned/magiclink?token=:magicLinkToken).

message
This information will be stored with the Magic Link and available in the response from Retrieve a Magic Link (/rp/api/versioned/magiclink?token=:magicLinkToken).

secondsValid
By default, Magic Links expire 24 hours (86400 seconds) after creation. To change the validity period, enter your preferred duration in seconds. For example, use 600 if you want the link to expire after 10 minutes.

mobileDeepLinkPrefix
This is the specific domain for the Device Manager instance which will be the destination of your Magic Link. The Domain Prefix is configurable in case your public-facing domain is different from your internal domain. For example, if your Device Manager instance is behind a firewall or DNS, you can enter the specific URL in this field. By default this will be blank and the mobileDeepLink that gets generated will start with hypr://register.

hyprServerUrl
This should be a link to your HYPR Control Center. The HYPR Mobile App will use this to determine where to send the registration request. This affects webLink, mobileDeepLink, and firebaseDynamicLinkForHyprApp in the response body.

registrationsLimit
This is the number of times the generated Magic Link can be used for registration. The default value is 1.

sessionAuthLimit
The maximum number of authentication attempts that can be made with this session.

setHyprServerUrlAsDefault
Do you want your HYPR tenant URL to be the default URL for this Magic Link?
[ true | false ]

sessionId
The unique identifier for the Magic Link session.

The following firebase* parameters are customzeable. HYPR default values are shown here.

firebaseDomainUrlPrefix
The subdomain as described in Manually constructing a Dynamic Link URL. The default value is https://hyprapp.page.link.

firebaseDeepLinkPrefix
The your_deep_link value as described in Manually constructing a Dynamic Link URL. The default value is https://hypr.com/dynamiclink.

firebaseAndroidPackageName
The package name of the Android app to use to open the deep link. This corresponds to the apn value as described in Manually constructing a Dynamic Link URL. The default is com.hypr.one.

firebaseAndroidVersionCode
The versionCode of the minimum version of your app that can open the link. This corresponds to the amv value as described in Manually constructing a Dynamic Link URL. The default is 1.

firebaseIOSBundleId
The bundle ID of the iOS app to use to open the link. The ibi value as described in Manually constructing a Dynamic Link URL. The default is com.hypr.one.

firebaseIOSAppStoreId
Your app's App Store ID, used to send users to the App Store when the app isn't installed. The isi value as described in Manually constructing a Dynamic Link URL. The default is 1343368858.

firebaseIOSCustomScheme
Your app's custom URL scheme, if defined to be something other than your app's bundle ID. The ius value as described in Manually constructing a Dynamic Link URL. The default is hypr.

firebaseSuffixOption
A short dynamic link suffix, if desired. defaults to null.

Response Body

{
  "rpAppId": "string",
  "username": "string",
  "firstname": "string",
  "lastname": "string",
  "email": "string",
  "webLink": "url",
  "mobileDeepLink": "url",
  "message": "string",
  "firebaseDynamicLinkForHyprApp": "url",
  "createTimeUTC": "timestamp",
  "expirationTimeUTC": "timestamp",
  "usedOnTimeUTC": "",
  "token": "string"
}

rpAppId
The camel case unique RP application identifier.

username
This is the username you supplied in the request.

firstname
This is the firstname you supplied in the request.

lastname
This is the lastname you supplied in the request.

email
This is the email you supplied in the request.

message
This is the message you supplied in the request.

webLink
The Web Link is designed to be opened in a computer browser and will take users to the HYPR Device Manager where they can begin the device registration process by scanning a QR code.

mobileDeepLink
This is a registration link to the Control Center instance which will be the destination of your dynamic link.

firebaseDynamicLinkForHyprApp
The dynamic link is intended to be opened on a mobile device where they will initiate the registration process directly in the HYPR Mobile App. Dynamic links also work as a normal web link if opened in a computer browser.

createTimeUTC
UTC creation time in Unix Epoch timestamp format.

expirationTimeUTC
UTC expiration time in Unix Epoch timestamp format.

usedOnTimeUTC
This will be null in the response.

token
This token can be used in subsequent Magic Links API calls to identify this Magic Link.

request.description:
Get the Entra ID information for the specified rpAppId (the integration's RP App in Control Center Advanced Mode) and upn values.

Based on the rpAppId, the HYPR Entra ID integration will provide the client ID, tentant ID, and secrets necessary to connect.

The Bearer Token must be the integration RP application token.

Added in HYPR version 9.3.0.

Status Codes

200 OK
Indicates success.

Path Parameters

rpAppId
The unique identifier for the RP application.

upn
The user principal name, typically in email format.

Request Body

The Request Body is empty.

Response Body

{
  "@odata.context": "<string>",
  "challengeTimeoutDateTime": <datetime>,
  "publicKey": {
    "challenge": "",
    "timeout": <integer>,
    "attestation": "<string>",
    "rp": {
      "id": "<string>",
      "name": "<string>"
    },
    "user": {
      "id": "<string>",
      "displayName": "<string>",
      "name": "<string>"
    },
    "pubKeyCredParams": [
      {
        "type": "<string>",
        "alg": <integer>
      },
      {
        "type": "<string>",
        "alg": <integer>
      }
    ],
    "excludeCredentials": [
    ],
    "authenticatorSelection": {
      "authenticatorAttachment": "<string>",
      "requireResidentKey": <boolean>,
      "userVerification": "<string>"
    },
    "extensions": {
      "hmacCreateSecret": <boolean>,
      "enforceCredentialProtectionPolicy": <boolean>,
      "credentialProtectionPolicy": "<string>"
    }
  }
}

@odata.context
The Microsoft Graph URL and metadata.

challengeTimeoutDateTime
Time stamp for the challenge timeout.

publicKey
An array of public key attributes.

  • challenge: The challenge contents.

  • timeout: Number of seconds before the challenge times out.

  • attestation: The type of attestation. [ NONE | DIRECT | INDIRECT | ENTERPRISE ]

  • rp: An array of relying party attributes.

    • id: The identifier for the relying party. Typically this will be login.microsoft.com.

    • name: The name of the relying party. Typically this will be Microsoft.

  • user: An array of user attributes.

    • id: The unique identifier for the Entra user.

    • displayName: The user's display name from Entra.

    • name: The user's name in Entra. Typically this will be in email format.

  • pubKeyCredParams: A data object housing one or more public key credential parameters, each with the type and alg attributes.

    • type: The type of public key. In this call, this value will always be public-key.

    • alg: The identifying algorithm number.

  • excludeCredentials

    • type: The type of public key. In this call, this value will always be public-key.

    • id: Theunique identifier for the credential.

    • transports: The means by which the credential is delivered.
      BLE: Bluetooth low energy
      HYBRID: Multiple transports, like a computer authenticating via a smart phone or tablet
      INTERNAL: The credential is bound to the hardware, like a secure element in a PC
      NFC: Near-field communications
      SMART-CARD: Chip-enabled cards
      USB: Credentials bound to a USB key

  • authenticatorSelection: An array containing selection attributes.

    • authenticatorAttachment: What is the authenticator form factor? [ CROSS-PLATFORM | PLATFORM ]

    • requireResidentKey: Is a resident key required? [ true | false ]

    • userVerification: How important is user verification? Default is PREFERRED. [ DISCOURAGED | PREFERRED | REQUIRED ]

  • extensions: An array containing extension attributes.

    • hmacCreateSecret: Create an HMAC secret? [ true | false ]

    • enforceCredentialProtectionPolicy: Determined whether or not the credentialProtectionPolicy will be used. [ true | false ]

    • credentialProtectionPolicy: The policy set by the browser; enabled by the previous attribute.

response.name: 200 OK

item.name: FIDO API
Start FIDO registration, authentication, or deregistration.

request.description:
Initiate FIDO registration, authentication, or deregistration.

The Bearer Token determines the affected RP application; this may be the controlCenterAdmin token.

Added in HYPR version 7.3.0.

Status Codes

200 OK

Request Body Parameters

session
Session information related to what is being registered, authorized, or deregistered.

  • machine: The unique identifier for the machine. Can be no more than 256 characters.

  • deviceId: Takes either the mobile device id or a smart key id. Can be no more than 256 characters.

  • sessionId: Typically registration is initiated via some other call. Can be no more than 256 characters. HYPR wraps a FIDO registration inside a HYPR specific registration to set up the association between mobile device, machine, etc. The sessionId is created via that other call, typically Client (web | workstation ) setup /rp/wsapi/client/setup.

  • machineUserName: For workstation registrations, the specific machine username.

fidoPayload
The FIDO-specific payload. The structure is defined by the FIDO standard.

  • context: Additional information for the FIDO operation.

    • transaction: TBD.

    • userName: The FIDO-specific username to register.

  • op: The FIDO operation to perform. [ Auth | Dereg | Reg ]

  • extras: A map of additional values. These values vary depending on the value of op, but typically will include the following:

    • appId: The camel case unique RP application identifier. This should be the same RP application to which the bearer token belongs. If FIDO FacetIDs are in use, this will be the /facets URL for the RP Application.

    • actionId: The name of the policy for the associated operation.

Response Body

{
  "status": {
    "responseCode": <integer>,
    "responseMessage": "<string>"
  },
  "response": {
    "version": <integer>,
    "sessionId": "<string>",
    "fidoResponse": {
      "uafRequest": "<string>",
      "statusCode": <integer>
    }
  }
}

status
An array containing HTTP status data.

  • responseCode: The embedded HTTP response code.

  • responseMessage: Additional status information.

response
An array containing response data.

  • version: The message body version. Default is 4.

  • sessionId: The unique identifier for the session.

  • fidoResponse: The FIDO response is returned in a FIDO UAF JSON blob.

    • uafRequest: A FIDO UAF JSON blob which contains header information, the policy (allowed authenticators by aaid), the challenge, and the sessionId. The challenge must be used in the assertion. The policy dictates which authenticators can be present in the assertion. The sessionId is used to associate this registration session with server side information. See the FIDO specification for complete details.

    • statusCode: A FIDO-specific status code. See the FIDO specification for details.

request.description:
Retrieves FIDO2 device metadata info from HYPR FIDO2 metadata service (MDS).

The Bearer Token must be the controlCenterAdmin token.

Added in HYPR version 7.2.0.

Status Codes

200 OK
Indicates success.

Request Body

The Request Body is empty.

Response Body

[
    {
        "id": <long>,
        "aaguid": "<string>",
        "tocNumber": "<string>",
        "description": "<string>",
        "version": <integer>,
        "source": "<string>",
        "enabled": <boolean>,
        "category": "<string>",
        "effectiveStatus": "<string>",
        "metadata": "<string>",
        "createDateInUTC": <datetime>,
        "updatedDateInUTC": <datetime>,
        "nextUpdateDate": <datetime>
    },
    {
        ...
    }
]

The response is a list of authenticators.

id
A unique identifier for the authenticator.

aaguid
The authenticator attestation global unique identifier (aaguid) for the authenticator.

tocNumber
If the source value is METADATA_SERVICE, tocNumber will reflect the serial number (no) from MetadataTOCPayload provided by the FIDO Alliance. If the source value is MANUAL_UPLOAD, tocNumber will be null.

description
A free-form field for describing the aaguid; typically this will be used to indicate the authenticator vendor.

version
The version of this aaguid as provided in the authenticatorVersion property in the MDS.

source
From where did the metadata come?
[ METADATA_SERVICE | MANUAL_UPLOAD ]

enabled
Is this aaguid enabled? This field may be false if a status update, such as a compromised account warning, has changed it. It may also be updated manually to enable or disable the authenticator.
[ true | false ]

category
This field is not used. [ null ]

effectiveStatus
Provided by the StatusReport attribute of the MetadataTOCPayloadEntry, if sourced from the external service. If this value is uploaded manually, it will be set by HYPR.

metatdata
Every item in the list includes a metadata field which contains a metadata statement for particular FIDO2 device in metadata statement format.

createDateInUTC
The date this aaguid was created; listed in UTC format.

updateDateInUTC
The date this aaguid was updated; listed in UTC format.

nextUpdateDate
The next date this aaguid will be updated; listed in UTC format. This value is provided by the nextUpdate attribute of MetadataTOCPayload, if sourced from MDS. If this value is uploaded manually, it is set by HYPR.

The Request Body is empty. Only the aaguid value in the path is needed.

Response Body

The Response Body is empty. Check the Status Codes for indicators of success or failure.

request.description:
First part of FIDO2 authentication flow, in which HYPR generates public key request options for the navigator.credentials.get JavaScript call. See the FIDO2 specification for reference.

The Bearer Token determines the affected RP application; this may be the controlCenterAdmin token.

Added in HYPR version 6.6.0.

Status Codes

200 OK

Request Body Parameters

username
The FIDO2 username, which may be different from the HYPR username.

userVerification
Enforce a requirement for User Verification (UV), such as PIN + Face ID or Fingerprint only. Acceptable values:

  • Required: The Relying Party requires user verification for the operation and will fail if the response does not have the user verification flag set.
  • Preferred: The Relying Party prefers user verification for the operation if possible, but will not fail the operation if the response does not have the user verification flag set.
  • Discouraged: The Relying Party does not want user verification.

authenticationSelectionA data object to qualify the authenticator.

  • authenticatorAttachment: The device housing the authenticator. [ platform | cross-platform ]

Response Body

{
    "status": "string",
    "errorMessage": "string",
    "challenge": "string",
    "timeout": int,
    "extensions": {
        "devicePubKey": {
            "attestation": "string",
            "attestationFormats": [
               null
            ]
        }
    },
    "rpId": "string",
    "userVerification": "string",
    "attestation": "string",
    "allowCredentials": [
        {
            "type": "string",
            "id": "string",
            "transports": [
                "string",
                "string"

        }

status
The status of the request.
[ ok | failed ]

errorMessage
Additional information about the request.

challenge
A random number sent from the server to be signed.

timeout
The Assertion Timeout as governed in FIDO2 Settings in the UI. Minimum value is _30000 (30 seconds).

extensions
An array for assertion extensions.

  • devicePubKey: An array governing device public key assertion values.
    • attestation: The type of attestation used by this assertion.
      • Direct: The Relying Party wants to receive an attestation statement that may include uniquely identifying information.
      • Indirect: This indicates that the Relying Party wants to receive the attestation statement as generated by the authenticator.
      • None: This indicates that the Relying Party is not interested in authenticator attestation.
    • attestationFormats: Currently not used.

rpId
The URL of the FIDO2 server.

userVerification
The same value echoed back from the request body (see above).

attestation
The type of attestation used by this assertion. See above.

allowCredentials
A data object containing credential values.

  • type: The type of credential. This value is always public-key.
  • id: The unique identifier for the credential.
  • transports: The method used by the FIDO device to connect. [ usb | nfc | ble | smart-card | hybrid | internal ]

request.description:
Second part of FIDO2 authentication flow, in which an authentication assertion is sent to HYPR for validation.

The Bearer Token determines the affected RP application; this may be the controlCenterAdmin token.

Added in HYPR version 6.6.0.

Returning the authenticator AAGUID

Add the optional requestMeta query parameter to have the server include metadata
about the credential in the result.

Value Meaning
0 (default) No metadata. The response is unchanged and fully backward compatible.
1 Include the credential's aaguid.

requestMeta is a bit-flag field. Future metadata fields use additional bits
(2, 4, and so on) and can be combined with a bitwise OR.

With requestMeta=1, a successful response includes a meta object:

{
  "status": "ok",
  "errorMessage": "",
  "username": "jdoe",
  "meta": {
    "aaguid": "01020304050607080102030405060708"
  }
}

aaguid is the authenticator's AAGUID as a 32-character hexadecimal string, without
dashes. It identifies the authenticator make and model, and can be cross-referenced
against the FIDO Alliance Metadata Service.

The meta object is omitted, and the response falls back to the standard payload, when:

  • requestMeta is omitted or set to 0; or

  • the authentication failed — metadata is never attached to a failed result.

Available in HYPR Server 11.3.0 and later.

For the full walkthrough, see
Retrieving the Authenticator AAGUID.

Status Codes

200 OK

Request Body

See the FIDO2 specification for reference.

Response Body

See the FIDO2 specification for reference.

description.content: Optional bit-flag controlling which metadata the server adds to the assertion result. 0 (default) returns the standard response, unchanged and backward compatible. 1 includes the credential's aaguid. Future metadata fields use additional bits (2, 4, …) and combine with a bitwise OR. Available in HYPR Server 11.3.0 and later.

request.description:
Delete (de-register) a single RP application user's FIDO2 device, or delete all fido2KeyId values associated with a user.

The Bearer Token determines the affected RP application; this may be the controlCenterAdmin token.

Added in HYPR 6.13.0.

Added deleteUser parameter in HYPR 10.3.1+

Status Codes

200 OKIndicates Success.

400 Bad Request
Returned when:

  • The device is not registered with that RP application fido2Username

  • The fido2Username does not exist

  • An invalid value has been used for any parameter

401 Unauthorized
Indicates an incorrect token or lack of access. The Response Body will be empty for this response.

Path Parameters

fido2Username (string)
The FIDO2 username, which may differ from the HYPR username.

fido2KeyId (string)
The unique FIDO2 key identifier.

deleteUser (boolean | optional)

When specified true, also deletes the user if it's the last device being deleted. False by default.

Request Body

Whether or not fido2Username is specified, if fido2KeyId is provided, that fido2KeyId will be removed from the RP application user's account. Only one fido2KeyId can be specified in the request.

If only the fido2Username is specified, all fido2KeyId values associated with that fido2Username will be removed.

request.description:
Returns RADIUS server status/stats for the specified radiusServerId within appId.

The Bearer Token should be specific to the RP application associated with the desired RADIUS integration.

Added in HYPR version 7.6.0.

Status Codes

200 OK

Path Parameters

rpAppId (string)
The camel case unique RP application identifier. This is the same as the rpAppId returned in Get RADIUS integrations (GET /rp/api/radius/integration).

radiusServerId (long)
The unique identifier assigned to each of the integration's servers. This corresponds to the Server ID column under the main RADIUS Integration page in Control Center.

Request Body

The Request Body is empty.

  "configuration": {
    "controlCenterInterval": <integer>,

    "proxyPort": <integer>,

    "proxyPassword": "<string>",
    "customAttributeName": "<string>",

  "threadPoolStats": {
    "authenticationAcceptCountTotal": <long>,
    "authenticationCountTotal": <long>,

    "threadPoolQueueSize": <long>,
    "threadPoolSize": <long>,

    "threadsQueued": <long>,
    "threadsRunning": <long>,
    "threadsScheduledTotal": <long>
  },
  "updatedAt": <datetime>,
  "radiusServerId": <long>
}

configuration
An array containing RADIUS server-specific information.

  • controlCenterInterval: The frequency that Control Center polls the server to check for updates.

  • timeoutSeconds: The number of seconds before an API authentication or configuration request is abandoned. Default is 60.

  • radiusConfigName: The human-readable name given to the configuration.

  • description: The description given to the configuration at creation.

  • radiusDomain: The domain to which the RADIUS server belongs.

  • localRadiusSecret: The RADIUS secret as determined at creation.

  • clientSecrets: An array of clients and their secrets.

    • [label]: The name of the client.

    • [value]: The client secret.

  • radiusTimeout: Number of seconds before the RADIUS polling times out.

  • rpUrl: The RADIUS RP application URL on the HYPR tenant.

  • rpAppId: The camel case unique RP application identifier for the RADIUS integration being queried.

  • accessToken: The RADIUS RP application access token.

  • proxyEnabled: Is this configuration employing a proxy server? [ true | false ]

  • proxyHost: The URL of the proxy server.

  • proxyPort: The port used by the host server for proxy transactions.

  • proxyUsername: The account username to connect to the proxyHost.

  • proxyPassword: the password matching the proxyUsername.

  • customAttributeName: Specific authentication, authorization, and accounting (AAA) elements in a user profile. See the HYPR RADIUS Custom Attributes article for options.

  • customAttributeValue: The value associated with the customAttributeName, above. This field must comply with the datatype for the chosen attribute.

threadPoolStats
A data object containing statistical information about the RADIUS server being queried.

  • threadsRunning: The total number of currently runnint threads.

  • threadsScheduledTotal: The total number of scheduled threads.

  • threadsCompletedTotal: The total number of completed threads.

  • threadsQueued: The total number of queued threads.

  • threadPoolSize: The current thread pool size.

  • threadPoolCoreSize: The current core thread pool size.

  • threadPoolQueueSize: the current thread pool queue size.

  • authenticationsRunning: The total number of currently running authentications.

  • authenticationsRunningMax: The maximum number of running authentications.

  • authenticationCountTotal: The total number of authentications.

  • authenticationAcceptCountTotal: The total number of successful authentications.

  • authenticationRejectCountTotal: The total number of rejected authentications.

  • authenticationTimeAverage: The average time taken to authenticate, in milliseconds.

  • authenticationTimeMax: The longest time taken to authenticate, in milliseconds.

updatesAt
The next scheduled poll of the RADIUS components.

radiusServerId
The unique identifier for the RADIUS server.

request.description:
Returns a list of entities that can be appended to this endpoint to get information about that entity.

The Bearer Token determines the affected RP application; this may be the controlCenterAdmin token.

Added in HYPR version 8.4.0.

Status Codes

200 OK

Path Parameters

entity
The property targeted by the bulk query. The value displayed here is appended to the endpoint and used to generate a list of fields (q.v.) governing that entity (e.g., /cc/api/bulk/introspect/machines) Possible values include the following:

  • apitoken: Endpoint API tokens

  • controlpoints: Platform control points

  • deleted_certificates: Certificates which need to be revoked by the issuer (Active Directory Certificate Services or CA)

  • deleted_registrations: Deleted registrations (combination of user, device, machine)

  • devices: Mobile/security keys

  • enrolledcredentials: Registration credential info

  • events: Audit Trail Events

  • featureflags: Feature flags

  • fido2authmd: FIDO2 authenticator metadata

  • fido2user: FIDO2 user registrations

  • firebaseinfo: Device-specific Firebase information

  • IdentityVerificationOIDCClientConfig: IDV OIDC Client configurations

  • idvcodecustomization: IDV code customizations

  • idvworkflowconfiguration: IDV workflow configurations

  • machines: Client website or workstation

  • magiclinks: Magic Link information

  • maintenance_state: Maintenance state table

  • requested_certificates: Valid certificates issued by the ADCS

  • registrations: A combination of user, device, and machine information

  • rpappconfig: RP application configurations

  • rpuserproperty: User properties

  • rp_workstation_detail: Machine data

  • securitykey: Security keys

  • serverconfig: General server configuration

  • sessions: Authentication sessions

  • signals: Device signal data

  • uafapplication: UAF application

  • uafauthenticator: UAF authenticators

  • uafloginaction: UAF policies

  • uafusers: FIDO users

  • useralias: User alias mapping

  • useremailmap: Username-to-email mapping

  • users: Registered users

  • webtowsmap: Web-to-workstation user map

  • wswebreg: WFA and web registration association

rpAppId
The camel case unique RP application identifier.

Request Body

The Request Body is empty.

Response Body

"status": "ok",
"entities": [
  {
    "name": "string",
    "description": "string"
  }
],
"fields": {
  "{{entity}}": [
    {
      "name": "string",
      "description": "string",
      "fieldtype": "string",
      "operations": "string"
    }
  ]
}

status
The status of the request. This mirrors the HTTP status code.

entities
The list of acceptable entities that can be queried.

fields
An array of the applicable fields for each entity. The entity name will be the next-level item (in our example, it would be machines).

  • name: The field label, such as deviceId or machineUserName.

  • description: A brief description of the field's function.

  • fieldtype: The datatype associated with the field (e.g., timestamp, boolean, string, etc.)

  • operations: Accepted operations on this field. This may include one or more of the following: GT, LT, EQ, or LIKE

Using allowed entities and fields from /cc/api/bulk/introspect, get the named fields for each returned instance of that entity.

Requires the Control Center API access token.

Added in HYPR version 8.4.0.

Status Codes

200 OK

Path Parameters

rpAppId
The camel case unique RP application identifier.

Request Body

{
    "target": {
        "subject": "string",
        "fields": [
            "string",
            "string",
            ...
        ]
    },
    "pagination": {
        "page": int,
        "rows": int
    }
}

target
An array denoting which entity to return and which fields for that entity.

  • subject: The entity about which you wish to get fields.
  • fields: The entity's fields that you wish reported.

pagination
An array governing the pages and rows to be displayed in the output. This object can be omitted to retrieve how many records exist.

  • page: Which page from your total output you would like returned, based on how many rows per page.
  • rows: How many rows will comprise a page.

Response Body

{
  "status": "string",
  "count": int,
  "cost": int,
  "results": [
    {
      "{{field1}}": "value1",
      "{{field2}}": "value2",
      "{{field3}}": "value3",      
      ...
    },
  ]
}

status
The status of the request. This mirrors the HTTP status code.

count
Will return null if pagination (above) is used. If pagination is omitted, the count returns the number of available records.

cost
A numeric representation of the cost to make the request; typically double the number of requested rows.

results
An array for each returned instance containing the fields chosen in the Request Body.

item.name: Obtain a list of throttled endpoints.

request.description:
Returns information about all known throttled endpoints.

This call requres a controlCenterAdmin access token.

Added in HYPR version 8.4.0.

Status Codes

200 OK

Request Body

The Request Body is empty.

Response Body

{
  "configs": [
    {
      "enabled": <boolean>,
      "configpath": "<string>",
      "capacity": <integer>,
      "timePeriod": "<duration>",
      "available": <integer>,
      "clustered": <boolean>,
      "defaultHttpStatus": <integer>,
      "configsrc": "<string>",
      "endpoints": [
        {
          "apipath": "<string>",
          "costDescription": "<string>"
        },
        {
          . . . 
        }
      ]
    }
    {
      . . . 
    }
  ]
}

configs
A data object containing a list of endpoints and throttling configuration data.

  • enabled: Is throttling enabled for this configuration? [ true | false ]
  • configpath: The relative path to the throttled endpoint.
  • capacity: Default capacity for this endpoint. If configsrc is static, then the capacity is in terms of calls. If configsrc is dynamic, the capacity is in costing units.
  • timePeriod: A multi-part variable, InternalBucketPathConfig, containing the following options mirroring the other Response Body values:
    • enabled: As above.
    • path: configpath, as above.
    • capacity: As above.
    • period: A duration formatted period of time. See ISO 8601 Durations.
    • clustered: As above.
    • throttleCode: If set, this value is used as the HTTP Status Code. This must be a valid code.
    • configsrc: As above.
  • available: Indicates whether or not the endpoint is available for throttling. [ true | false ]
  • clustered: Clustered or local capacity? If clustered, then this endpoint capacity is evaluated at Redis (requires a Redis call). If local then this endpoint is only evaluated locally. Defaults to true (clustered). In a clustered environment, the effective capacity of a local capacity endpoint is calculated as [configured capacity]/[number of nodes present]. [ true | false ]
  • defaultHttpStatus: The default throttling status recorded to the log stream. Default is 429 TOO_MANY_REQUESTS.
  • configsrc: The endpoint path is either explicitly specified (via annotation expath; static) or implicitly derived (from the controller relative URL; dynamic).
    [ dynamic | static ]
  • endpoints
    • apipath: The endpoint path; used for the status field.
    • costDescription: The description of the cost. If set to "", we assume a fixed cost of 1.
